On Sunday, November 8, Nvidia’s board launched an independent investigation after reports that Huang was targeted by a Chinese spy operation; Huang admitted to an affair with Alice Huang, a former executive at Singapore-based chip company Megaspeed. Nvidia’s influence extends far beyond the United States. The chip giant has built close ties with companies worldwide, particularly in Asia, where many of its key partners play important roles in the global AI industry. China’s foreign ministry rejected allegations on November 10 that a Chinese businesswoman linked to former Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang was a spy, calling them groundless and a smear against Beijing. On Friday , a spokesperson reiterated opposition to export controls that disrupt global supply chains and stated the ministry was not aware of reports linking restricted Nvidia chips to a Shanghai data center associated with Alice Huang. Huang’s exit has also raised uncertainty over more than $3 billion in Chinese AI computing projects reliant on Nvidia’s restricted processors, according to Reuters. Many of these chips are subject to U.S. export controls, making them difficult for Chinese companies to obtain. In Singapore, authorities seized the passport of Alice Huang, former CEO of Singapore-based cloud computing company Megaspeed, in June 2025 as part of an investigation into possible false declarations regarding server purchases, according to the Ministry of Home Affairs. The Singapore ministry said police took her passport to ensure she remained available for questioning, as she was not based in Singapore. The investigation examined whether servers shipped from Singapore to Malaysia were later sent to other countries without proper declaration. In February 2026, police found insufficient evidence to establish that Alice Huang had committed offenses related to the suspected false declarations, according to the ministry. However, authorities said she had knowingly provided inaccurate information about her role at Megaspeed. She was issued a warning and barred from re-entering Singapore. Her passport was returned that month. Singapore also said it received limited assistance from U.S. authorities despite repeated requests for information about U.S. server maker Supermicro. Singapore’s Ministry of Home Affairs said its investigation into Megaspeed and six other individuals remains ongoing. The ministry did not identify the six individuals or specify their alleged roles in the case. South Korea has close ties to Nvidia, with major chipmakers Samsung Electronics and SK Hynix playing important roles in supplying memory chips used in its AI processors. Apart from that, South Korea’s government AI strategy council held an emergency meeting on Friday to assess the potential impact of Huang’s departure on the country’s AI industry, per a local media report. Taiwan’s Economy Minister Kung Ming-shin said Huang’s departure was unlikely to significantly change the growth of the global AI industry, according to local media . Meanwhile, Taipei’s city government said Nvidia’s planned overseas headquarters in the city remained on track despite the leadership change. The company has met its contractual obligations so far, and officials said they would continue to support the project. In Japan, the Industry Ministry said the government would closely monitor Nvidia following Huang’s resignation, describing the chipmaker as an important player in Japan’s AI semiconductor industry, Reuters reported. Deputy chief cabinet secretary Masanao Ozaki said it was too early to assess the impact on the global AI industry, while stressing Japan’s commitment to ensuring a stable supply of semiconductors. Because every Nvidia chip a Chinese company buys is one that Huawei or Cambricon doesn't sell, and domestic chips can only catch up if people actually buy them (which means money for R&D, etc.). Which means that the notion that Chinese intelligence was running honeytraps to get more Nvidia chips into China gets the whole thing exactly backwards. In fact, it looks like Megaspeed - Alice Huang's company - was a counter-reaction to official Chinese policy: a private sector workaround to these efforts by the Chinese government to curtail Nvidia. That is a backdoor not only - allegedly - around Washington's export controls, but also around China's own efforts to wean its companies off Nvidia. I can't believe the Chinese government was too thrilled about it: it'd make just about zero sense for it to run countless domestic measures to prevent Alibaba from using Nvidia chips, yet at the same time have its top spy agency help the same Alibaba get Nvidia chips through the back door in Southeast Asia ???? Who benefitted is pretty clear: - Nvidia itself: it's in the business of selling chips so a customer willing to spend billions of dollars on chips in Southeast Asia is a godsend. Who does NOT benefit, according to official Chinese policy, is the Chinese state, which has made tech self-reliance one of its foremost priorities. Which means that, to believe the spy story, you have to believe that a person - Alice Huang - was effectively a spy paid by her own government while simultaneously sabotaging its tech self-reliance drive, which it has spent years and trillions of dollars on - pretty senseless. extraction.body: Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang resigned Thursday after his extramarital affair with a Chinese businesswoman who reportedly was also acting as a spy for Beijing raised U.S. national security concerns. The company named Colette Kress as interim CEO . She had been Nvidia’s executive vice president and chief financial officer. Huang’s resignation comes after Nvidia’s board gathered to discuss his future following revelations that he was having an affair with Alice Huang , a former executive at Singapore-based Megaspeed International suspected of spying for China. The two aren’t related. The New York Times reported Wednesday that Huang also had an affair with an Nvidia executive who reported to him. The Associated Press could not independently confirm those reports. Shares of Nvidia, one of the largest companies in the world, fell sharply at the opening bell Thursday. Huang’s departure is a test for the AI industry Stephanie Balaouras, group research director for research firm Forrester, said Jensen Huang’s resignation from chip-maker Nvidia isn’t just a test for the company but the AI boom as a whole. “If Nvidia stabilizes quickly under new leadership, the AI infrastructure boom will have demonstrated resilience. If its stock, financing relationships, or ecosystem commitments remain under sustained pressure, that would add evidence to the fragile side of the AI bubble ledger,” she said. “Tech leaders shouldn’t overreact, but they should treat Nvidia’s CEO transition as a prompt to reassess concentration risk across their AI infrastructure, suppliers, and investment plans.” Nvidia shares fell after the company announced Jensen Huang’s resignation as CEO. The New York Times reported Wednesday that Huang also had an affair with an Nvidia executive who reported to him. The Associated Press could not independently confirm those reports.
Shares of Nvidia, one of the largest companies in the world, fell sharply at the opening bell Thursday.
Huang’s departure is a test for the AI industry
Stephanie Balaouras, group research director for research firm Forrester, said Jensen Huang’s resignation from chip-maker Nvidia isn’t just a test for the company but the AI boom as a whole.

“If Nvidia stabilizes quickly under new leadership, the AI infrastructure boom will have demonstrated resilience. If its stock, financing relationships, or ecosystem commitments remain under sustained pressure, that would add evidence to the fragile side of the AI bubble ledger,” she said. “Tech leaders shouldn’t overreact, but they should treat Nvidia’s CEO transition as a prompt to reassess concentration risk across their AI infrastructure, suppliers, and investment plans.”
Nvidia shares fell after the company announced Jensen Huang’s resignation as CEO.
After tumbling at the open of trading, Nvidia shares were down 5.3% as of 10:30 a.m. EST Thursday.

The chipmaker became the face of the AI boom under Huang’s leadership. The shares set a record high last month after soaring an astounding 1,722% in four years. But Nvidia’s share price has dropped more than 30% since then, initially on concerns the enthusiasm over AI was overdone and this past week on worries about whether Huang would remain with the company.

The S&P 500 fell 0.4%, and technology stocks were the biggest weights dragging down the benchmark index. Nvidia and several other tech companies have pricey stock values that tend to have more influence on the market’s direction. The tech-heavy Nasdaq fell 0.7%.

President Donald Trump has reacted to the resignation of Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang by saying that Huang “has done a fantastic job,” and adding, “There is only one man to take his place – TIM COOK of Apple.”
“A Legend replaces a Legend!” Trump wrote on his social media site of Cook, who is Apple’s former CEO.

Late Wednesday, media reports also said Huang had another extramarital affair with an Nvidia employee who reports to him. The FBI is investigating Huang’s affair with an alleged Chinese government agent .
The chipmaker “now has to prove it can maintain its AI dominance without the leader largely responsible for building it,” Hiken said.
“Given the broader AI industry’s heavy dependence on Nvidia’s chips, Huang’s departure introduces uncertainty well beyond the company itself,” he said.

“While Huang’s personal decisions are scandalous, his particular affair with an alleged Chinese spy raises much bigger questions about the security risks facing companies at the center of the AI race,” he said. “AI technology has become critical to U.S. national security, making even the personal relationships of industry leaders a potential vulnerability.”
Dan Ives, a technology analyst with the investment firm Yorkville Ives, said removing Jensen was a necessary step by the board of chipmaker Nvidia.

“The old Jensen, the black leather jacket, the Godfather of AI, the rock star viewed as the face of the AI boom, is over and in the past,” he wrote in a note to investors. “His value to the company pre- and post-this week is dramatically different, and the board did what we said it needed to do, which is rip off the band-aid and take Nvidia into its next chapter without him after this dark moment for Jensen and Nvidia.”

He still recommends investors buy Nvidia stock. He said Nvidia is still two to three years ahead of its nearest competitor and the “demand trajectory” for its chips isn’t changing because Jensen is gone.

The Nvidia spokesperson pushed back on the story in a statement to CNBC, saying that Singapore-based Megaspeed is another one of the company's regional cloud customers, and that Jensen Huang's interactions with its officials are not unusual, because he speaks with thousands of customers every year.
Earlier this year the U.S. government cleared Nvidia's H200 chip to be shipped to China, but Chinese regulators prevented their imports.
H200s are Nvidia's Hopper generation chip, not the current faster Blackwell generation currently used by American AI developers.
Last year, Nvidia wrote off about $4.5 billion in Chinese-tuned AI chips.
Nvidia said that Megaspeed had already been investigated for evading export controls.
The spokesperson added that customers don't get access to Nvidia trade secrets or relevant national security information.
Nvidia has had to walk a tightrope in Washington as its AI chips have become a powerful tool for all AI developers and a bargaining chip in economic competition with China.

On Friday , a spokesperson reiterated opposition to export controls that disrupt global supply chains and stated the ministry was not aware of reports linking restricted Nvidia chips to a Shanghai data center associated with Alice Huang.
Following Huang’s exit, South Korea’s Science Ministry said Nvidia had reaffirmed its plan to supply 260,000 advanced GPUs to the country and to continue joint AI projects.

Jensen Huang’s departure from Nvidia has drawn a range of responses across Asia, with some governments moving to confirm chip supply commitments, while others are monitoring the impact on local projects or addressing ongoing investigations.
Meanwhile, Taipei’s city government said Nvidia’s planned overseas headquarters in the city remained on track despite the leadership change.

"This is the biggest irony of the whole Alice Huang / Nvidia saga: the Chinese government actually doesn't want Nvidia chips and is actively keeping them out of the country," he wrote.Bertrand pointed to reports that Beijing had ordered Alibaba and ByteDance to cancel Nvidia orders and sent customs teams to ports to inspect advanced chips.This is the biggest irony of the whole Alice Huang / Nvidia saga: the Chinese government actually doesn't want Nvidia chips and is actively keeping them out of the country.

extraction.body: Jensen Huang’s departure from Nvidia has drawn a range of responses across Asia, with some governments moving to confirm chip supply commitments, while others are monitoring the impact on local projects or addressing ongoing investigations. On Sunday, November 8, Nvidia’s board launched an independent investigation after reports that Huang was targeted by a Chinese spy operation; Huang admitted to an affair with Alice Huang, a former executive at Singapore-based chip company Megaspeed. Nvidia’s influence extends far beyond the United States. The chip giant has built close ties with companies worldwide, particularly in Asia, where many of its key partners play important roles in the global AI industry. China’s foreign ministry rejected allegations on November 10 that a Chinese businesswoman linked to former Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang was a spy, calling them groundless and a smear against Beijing. On Friday , a spokesperson reiterated opposition to export controls that disrupt global supply chains and stated the ministry was not aware of reports linking restricted Nvidia chips to a Shanghai data center associated with Alice Huang. Huang’s exit has also raised uncertainty over more than $3 billion in Chinese AI computing projects reliant on Nvidia’s restricted processors, according to Reuters. Many of these chips are subject to U.S. export controls, making them difficult for Chinese companies to obtain. In Singapore, authorities seized the passport of Alice Huang, former CEO of Singapore-based cloud computing company Megaspeed, in June 2025 as part of an investigation into possible false declarations regarding server purchases, according to the Ministry of Home Affairs. The Singapore ministry said police took her passport to ensure she remained available for questioning, as she was not based in Singapore. The investigation examined whether servers shipped from Singapore to Malaysia were later sent to other countries without proper declaration. In February 2026, police found insufficient evidence to establish that Alice Huang had committed offenses related to the suspected false declarations, according to the ministry. However, authorities said she had knowingly provided inaccurate information about her role at Megaspeed. She was issued a warning and barred from re-entering Singapore. Her passport was returned that month. Singapore also said it received limited assistance from U.S. authorities despite repeated requests for information about U.S. server maker Supermicro. Singapore’s Ministry of Home Affairs said its investigation into Megaspeed and six other individuals remains ongoing. The ministry did not identify the six individuals or specify their alleged roles in the case. South Korea has close ties to Nvidia, with major chipmakers Samsung Electronics and SK Hynix playing important roles in supplying memory chips used in its AI processors. Following Huang’s exit, South Korea’s Science Ministry said Nvidia had reaffirmed its plan to supply 260,000 advanced GPUs to the country and to continue joint AI projects. Apart from that, South Korea’s government AI strategy council held an emergency meeting on Friday to assess the potential impact of Huang’s departure on the country’s AI industry, per a local media report. Taiwan’s Economy Minister Kung Ming-shin said Huang’s departure was unlikely to significantly change the growth of the global AI industry, according to local media . Meanwhile, Taipei’s city government said Nvidia’s planned overseas headquarters in the city remained on track despite the leadership change. The company has met its contractual obligations so far, and officials said they would continue to support the project. In Japan, the Industry Ministry said the government would closely monitor Nvidia following Huang’s resignation, describing the chipmaker as an important player in Japan’s AI semiconductor industry, Reuters reported. Deputy chief cabinet secretary Masanao Ozaki said it was too early to assess the impact on the global AI industry, while stressing Japan’s commitment to ensuring a stable supply of semiconductors. "This is the biggest irony of the whole Alice Huang / Nvidia saga: the Chinese government actually doesn't want Nvidia chips and is actively keeping them out of the country," he wrote.Bertrand pointed to reports that Beijing had ordered Alibaba and ByteDance to cancel Nvidia orders and sent customs teams to ports to inspect advanced chips.This is the biggest irony of the whole Alice Huang / Nvidia saga: the Chinese government actually doesn't want Nvidia chips and is actively keeping them out of the country. Because every Nvidia chip a Chinese company buys is one that Huawei or Cambricon doesn't sell, and domestic chips can only catch up if people actually buy them (which means money for R&D, etc.). Which means that the notion that Chinese intelligence was running honeytraps to get more Nvidia chips into China gets the whole thing exactly backwards. In fact, it looks like Megaspeed - Alice Huang's company - was a counter-reaction to official Chinese policy: a private sector workaround to these efforts by the Chinese government to curtail Nvidia. That is a backdoor not only - allegedly - around Washington's export controls, but also around China's own efforts to wean its companies off Nvidia. I can't believe the Chinese government was too thrilled about it: it'd make just about zero sense for it to run countless domestic measures to prevent Alibaba from using Nvidia chips, yet at the same time have its top spy agency help the same Alibaba get Nvidia chips through the back door in Southeast Asia ???? Who benefitted is pretty clear: - Nvidia itself: it's in the business of selling chips so a customer willing to spend billions of dollars on chips in Southeast Asia is a godsend. Who does NOT benefit, according to official Chinese policy, is the Chinese state, which has made tech self-reliance one of its foremost priorities. Which means that, to believe the spy story, you have to believe that a person - Alice Huang - was effectively a spy paid by her own government while simultaneously sabotaging its tech self-reliance drive, which it has spent years and trillions of dollars on - pretty senseless. Stranger things have happened, I guess, but it doesn't pass the smell test. extraction.body: Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang resigned Thursday after his extramarital affair with a Chinese businesswoman who reportedly was also acting as a spy for Beijing raised U.S. national security concerns. The company named Colette Kress as interim CEO . She had been Nvidia’s executive vice president and chief financial officer. Huang’s resignation comes after Nvidia’s board gathered to discuss his future following revelations that he was having an affair with Alice Huang , a former executive at Singapore-based Megaspeed International suspected of spying for China. The two aren’t related. The New York Times reported Wednesday that Huang also had an affair with an Nvidia executive who reported to him. The Associated Press could not independently confirm those reports. Shares of Nvidia, one of the largest companies in the world, fell sharply at the opening bell Thursday. Huang’s departure is a test for the AI industry Stephanie Balaouras, group research director for research firm Forrester, said Jensen Huang’s resignation from chip-maker Nvidia isn’t just a test for the company but the AI boom as a whole. “If Nvidia stabilizes quickly under new leadership, the AI infrastructure boom will have demonstrated resilience. If its stock, financing relationships, or ecosystem commitments remain under sustained pressure, that would add evidence to the fragile side of the AI bubble ledger,” she said. “Tech leaders shouldn’t overreact, but they should treat Nvidia’s CEO transition as a prompt to reassess concentration risk across their AI infrastructure, suppliers, and investment plans.” Nvidia shares fell after the company announced Jensen Huang’s resignation as CEO. After tumbling at the open of trading, Nvidia shares were down 5.3% as of 10:30 a.m. EST Thursday. The chipmaker became the face of the AI boom under Huang’s leadership. The shares set a record high last month after soaring an astounding 1,722% in four years. But Nvidia’s share price has dropped more than 30% since then, initially on concerns the enthusiasm over AI was overdone and this past week on worries about whether Huang would remain with the company. The S&P 500 fell 0.4%, and technology stocks were the biggest weights dragging down the benchmark index. Nvidia and several other tech companies have pricey stock values that tend to have more influence on the market’s direction. The tech-heavy Nasdaq fell 0.7%. Trump says his close ally Huang ‘did a fantastic job’ President Donald Trump has reacted to the resignation of Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang by saying that Huang “has done a fantastic job,” and adding, “There is only one man to take his place – TIM COOK of Apple.” “A Legend replaces a Legend!” Trump wrote on his social media site of Cook, who is Apple’s former CEO. Huang, who like a lot of top tech CEOs was close with Trump, left his post Thursday after his extramarital affair raised national security concerns. Huang faced growing calls to resign after his affair with an alleged Chinese spy. Late Wednesday, media reports also said Huang had another extramarital affair with an Nvidia employee who reports to him. The FBI is investigating Huang’s affair with an alleged Chinese government agent . The chipmaker “now has to prove it can maintain its AI dominance without the leader largely responsible for building it,” Hiken said. “Given the broader AI industry’s heavy dependence on Nvidia’s chips, Huang’s departure introduces uncertainty well beyond the company itself,” he said. “While Huang’s personal decisions are scandalous, his particular affair with an alleged Chinese spy raises much bigger questions about the security risks facing companies at the center of the AI race,” he said. “AI technology has become critical to U.S. national security, making even the personal relationships of industry leaders a potential vulnerability.” Dan Ives, a technology analyst with the investment firm Yorkville Ives, said removing Jensen was a necessary step by the board of chipmaker Nvidia. “The old Jensen, the black leather jacket, the Godfather of AI, the rock star viewed as the face of the AI boom, is over and in the past,” he wrote in a note to investors. “His value to the company pre- and post-this week is dramatically different, and the board did what we said it needed to do, which is rip off the band-aid and take Nvidia into its next chapter without him after this dark moment for Jensen and Nvidia.” He still recommends investors buy Nvidia stock. He said Nvidia is still two to three years ahead of its nearest competitor and the “demand trajectory” for its chips isn’t changing because Jensen is gone. Singapore says it has barred Alice Huang from returning to the country Singapore authorities said Thursday that they banned Alice Huang from returning to the country after opening an investigation into Megaspeed over “suspected false declarations” about server purchases. Investigators looked into whether servers were bought and exported through Singapore to neighboring Malaysia, and then routed to a final destination, contrary to what was declared in Singapore. Police in the Southeast Asian city-state investigated Alice Huang for “suspected involvement in the possible offences,” but not for espionage, according to a detailed statement issued by the Home Affairs Department. They seized her passport as part of investigation but returned it in February after concluding that “there was insufficient evidence” that she committed any offences. A plunge for Nvidia’s stock is pulling the U.S. market lower, threatening to upend the AI boom that has carried Wall Street to record after record in recent years. The S&P 500 fell 0.7% Thursday. The weakness in AI stocks sent the Nasdaq composite down 1.5%, while the Dow Jones Industrial Average added 127 points. Nvidia tumbled 14% after Jensen Huang, its co-founder and face of the brand, resigned as CEO. Other stocks in the AI industry also fell, though some of Nvidia’s rival chip companies rose. Oil prices swung after President Donald Trump said he’s no longer interested in a deal with Iran. Megaspeed says it is committed to working with the US government Megaspeed, the Singapore-headquartered data center company at the center of Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang’s scandal, pledged Thursday to cooperate with investigations into potential risks to U.S. national security. “Megaspeed is committed to working constructively and transparently with the U.S. government,” said the statement signed by its chairman and CEO, Tan Yong Pong, who also goes by James Tan. Nvidia has said it had “no reason to believe” that either national security or Nvidia secrets were compromised, but that its inquiry would examine all available information. Megaspeed faced claims last year that it was illicitly shipping advanced Nvidia computer chips into China, but in December said there was “no evidence” of such exports. Singapore has also said it is investigating such allegations. Shares slid more than 7% to $160.85 before the opening bell, 34% below the company’s all-time high reached just over a month ago. The New York Times reported Wednesday that Huang had a second affair with an Nvidia executive who reports to him, and analysts said that may force the board to oust him.

Stephanie Balaouras, group research director for research firm Forrester, said Jensen Huang’s resignation from chip-maker Nvidia isn’t just a test for the company but the AI boom as a whole.

“If Nvidia stabilizes quickly under new leadership, the AI infrastructure boom will have demonstrated resilience. But Nvidia’s share price has dropped more than 30% since then, initially on concerns the enthusiasm over AI was overdone and this past week on worries about whether Huang would remain with the company.

The S&P 500 fell 0.4%, and technology stocks were the biggest weights dragging down the benchmark index. Nvidia and several other tech companies have pricey stock values that tend to have more influence on the market’s direction. The tech-heavy Nasdaq fell 0.7%.
Trump says his close ally Huang ‘did a fantastic job’

President Donald Trump has reacted to the resignation of Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang by saying that Huang “has done a fantastic job,” and adding, “There is only one man to take his place – TIM COOK of Apple.”
“A Legend replaces a Legend!” Trump wrote on his social media site of Cook, who is Apple’s former CEO.

Huang, who like a lot of top tech CEOs was close with Trump, left his post Thursday after his extramarital affair raised national security concerns. Huang faced growing calls to resign after his affair with an alleged Chinese spy.

Late Wednesday, media reports also said Huang had another extramarital affair with an Nvidia employee who reports to him. The FBI is investigating Huang’s affair with an alleged Chinese government agent .
The chipmaker “now has to prove it can maintain its AI dominance without the leader largely responsible for building it,” Hiken said.
“Given the broader AI industry’s heavy dependence on Nvidia’s chips, Huang’s departure introduces uncertainty well beyond the company itself,” he said.

“While Huang’s personal decisions are scandalous, his particular affair with an alleged Chinese spy raises much bigger questions about the security risks facing companies at the center of the AI race,” he said. “AI technology has become critical to U.S. national security, making even the personal relationships of industry leaders a potential vulnerability.”
Dan Ives, a technology analyst with the investment firm Yorkville Ives, said removing Jensen was a necessary step by the board of chipmaker Nvidia.

“The old Jensen, the black leather jacket, the Godfather of AI, the rock star viewed as the face of the AI boom, is over and in the past,” he wrote in a note to investors. “His value to the company pre- and post-this week is dramatically different, and the board did what we said it needed to do, which is rip off the band-aid and take Nvidia into its next chapter without him after this dark moment for Jensen and Nvidia.”

He still recommends investors buy Nvidia stock. He said Nvidia is still two to three years ahead of its nearest competitor and the “demand trajectory” for its chips isn’t changing because Jensen is gone.
Singapore says it has barred Alice Huang from returning to the country

Singapore authorities said Thursday that they banned Alice Huang from returning to the country after opening an investigation into Megaspeed over “suspected false declarations” about server purchases.
Investigators looked into whether servers were bought and exported through Singapore to neighboring Malaysia, and then routed to a final destination, contrary to what was declared in Singapore.

Police in the Southeast Asian city-state investigated Alice Huang for “suspected involvement in the possible offences,” but not for espionage, according to a detailed statement issued by the Home Affairs Department.
They seized her passport as part of investigation but returned it in February after concluding that “there was insufficient evidence” that she committed any offences.
A plunge for Nvidia’s stock is pulling the U.S. market lower, threatening to upend the AI boom that has carried Wall Street to record after record in recent years.

The S&P 500 fell 0.7% Thursday. The weakness in AI stocks sent the Nasdaq composite down 1.5%, while the Dow Jones Industrial Average added 127 points. Megaspeed says it is committed to working with the US government

Megaspeed, the Singapore-headquartered data center company at the center of Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang’s scandal, pledged Thursday to cooperate with investigations into potential risks to U.S. national security.
“Megaspeed is committed to working constructively and transparently with the U.S. government,” said the statement signed by its chairman and CEO, Tan Yong Pong, who also goes by James Tan.
Nvidia has said it had “no reason to believe” that either national security or Nvidia secrets were compromised, but that its inquiry would examine all available information.

Megaspeed faced claims last year that it was illicitly shipping advanced Nvidia computer chips into China, but in December said there was “no evidence” of such exports. Singapore has also said it is investigating such allegations.

The development comes amid increasing pressure on Nvidia and CEO Jensen Huang in the U.S. over his efforts to ease restrictions on AI chip exports to China. The scrutiny has intensified following reports that Huang was allegedly targeted in a Chinese intelligence operation, with the CEO admitting to an affair.

The university's management school acquired the chips through Shaanxi Bosuan Network Technology, a third-party supplier, rather than buying them directly from Nvidia, the report added.

The Northwestern Polytechnical University obtained access to H200 chips and other high-performance Nvidia AI processors this year through five agreements with Chinese companies to rent computing capacity, the report noted. Nvidia's H200 ranks among its most powerful processors for developing and operating advanced AI models.

Exports of the chips require U.S. government approval, with licences generally refused for entities on the country's blacklist, including Northwestern Polytechnical University. The U.S. added Northwestern Polytechnical University to its Entity List in 2001 over alleged missile-proliferation and military research activities, tightening restrictions in 2019 by making export licence approvals for controlled U.S. technology generally subject to denial.
The Trump administration began allowing some H200 exports to China in January, but restrictions on Entity List institutions like Northwestern Polytechnical remained in place.

Beyond buying two H200 chips for its management school, Northwestern Polytechnical's cybersecurity school signed two seven-month agreements in January, worth 441,700 yuan and 441,000 yuan, to rent servers equipped with eight H200 chips each for AI model fine-tuning and reinforcement-learning training. The university also leased computing capacity powered by eight Nvidia A100 chips and eight A800 chips, both restricted from export to Chinese entities. The H200 remains the most advanced processor mentioned in its procurement records, according to the report.
Nvidia, the Commerce Department and its Bureau of Industry and Security did not immediately respond to Benzinga's request for comment.

Other Chinese universities also acquired restricted Nvidia processors. Shenzhen University purchased three H100 chips for 769,800 yuan in September, while Wuhan University of Technology purchased an H100-equipped server for 355,000 yuan in June and four A100 chips for another 344,000 yuan. Beihang University, part of China's "Seven Sons of National Defense," bought four A800 chips for 489,000 yuan in April. It has close ties to China's aerospace and defense sectors, the report noted.

sources.title: Exclusive-PLA-linked Chinese university bought Nvidia H200 chips despite US blacklist, records show - Centre Daily Times
passages: BEIJING, Nov 11 (Reuters) - A Chinese university with deep ties to the People's Liberation Army bought Nvidia's powerful H200 AI chips last month despite being on a US export blacklist, procurement records show, highlighting gaps in Washington's efforts to curb China's access to advanced technology.
Shenzhen University bought three H100 processors, another high-end Nvidia AI chip banned by the US, for 769,800 yuan in September.
Wuhan University of Technology bought a server containing an H100 chip for 355,000 yuan in June and four A100 chips in a separate 344,000 yuan purchase, the records show.

A Reuters review of 26 Chinese procurement and corporate records from this year found universities and research institutions buying US-restricted Nvidia chips or renting access to Nvidia-powered computing services that use such chips through domestic suppliers.
It also rented access to servers containing eight Nvidia A100 chips and eight A800 chips.
The A100 and A800 are banned from export to all Chinese entities, though the H200 is the most advanced of those cited in Northwestern Polytechnical's procurement records.
The US Commerce Department added the university to its trade blacklist, known as the Entity List, in 2001 over its alleged involvement in missile-proliferation activities and military research.

The January licensing rules also require safeguards to prevent blacklisted entities and military end-users from remotely accessing chips exported under the policy, which covers H200 processors and less advanced models.
Last week, Reuters reported that small quantities of H200 chips had reached China through indirect routes while Beijing withheld approval for large-scale imports.
Northwestern is a member of the "Seven Sons of National Defense" group of Chinese universities under U.S. sanctions and with a history of conducting defence-related research for Beijing.
The chips were purchased for its management school from Shaanxi Bosuan Network Technology rather than directly from Nvidia, the record shows.
The universities named in the records did not respond to requests for comment.

extraction.body: BEIJING, Nov 11 (Reuters) - A Chinese university with deep ties to the People's Liberation Army bought Nvidia's powerful H200 AI chips last month despite being on a US export blacklist, procurement records show, highlighting gaps in Washington's efforts to curb China's access to advanced technology. The findings come as Nvidia and its CEO Jensen Huang face mounting scrutiny in Washington over his lobbying for looser restrictions on sales of AI chips to China, following reports alleging he was targeted by a Chinese spying operation. Huang has argued that continued US sales to China would preserve American technological leadership and keep Chinese customers reliant on US technology. But some US lawmakers say access to Nvidia's most powerful AI chips can speed China's development of AI systems for weapons design, intelligence analysis and military modernisation. Both Democrats and Republicans in Congress have urged stronger controls on China's access to advanced AI chips, such as chip-tracking requirements and greater congressional oversight of exports. Three Republican congressional committee chairmen have requested a briefing with Huang on November 18 over his reported contacts with an alleged Chinese intelligence operative. Northwestern Polytechnical University bought two H200 chips last month for 874,700 yuan ($123,000), according to an October 21 procurement record on its website. Northwestern is a member of the "Seven Sons of National Defense" group of Chinese universities under U.S. sanctions and with a history of conducting defence-related research for Beijing. The chips were purchased for its management school from Shaanxi Bosuan Network Technology rather than directly from Nvidia, the record shows. The H200 is among Nvidia's most capable chips for training and running advanced AI systems and is subject to US export licence approvals, which are normally denied for blacklisted institutions such as Northwestern Polytechnical. Northwestern Polytechnical also bought access this year to H200 chips and other powerful Nvidia AI processors through five contracts for rented computing capacity from Chinese companies, procurement records show. Reuters is reporting the chip purchases and computing contracts for the first time. Northwestern Polytechnical, Nvidia and the US Commerce Department's Bureau of Industry and Security, which oversees export controls, did not respond to requests for comment. Reuters could not determine contact details for Shaanxi Bosuan Network Technology. Based in the northwestern city of Xian, Northwestern Polytechnical conducts research related to military aircraft, missiles and satellites. The US Commerce Department added the university to its trade blacklist, known as the Entity List, in 2001 over its alleged involvement in missile-proliferation activities and military research. It tightened the restrictions in 2019, making licences for exports of controlled US technology to the university subject to a policy of denial in most circumstances. Northwestern Polytechnical's purchases show how Chinese institutions with military ties continue to obtain US AI computing power through domestic suppliers, either by buying chips outright or renting access to servers containing them. A Reuters review of 26 Chinese procurement and corporate records from this year found universities and research institutions buying US-restricted Nvidia chips or renting access to Nvidia-powered computing services that use such chips through domestic suppliers. Several had close links to China's defence industry or military research. The universities named in the records did not respond to requests for comment. US President Donald Trump's administration began allowing some H200 exports to China on a case-by-case basis in January. But that policy did not lift the separate restrictions applying to Entity List organisations such as Northwestern Polytechnical. The January licensing rules also require safeguards to prevent blacklisted entities and military end-users from remotely accessing chips exported under the policy, which covers H200 processors and less advanced models. In addition to the management school's outright purchase of the two H200 chips, procurement records show the university's cybersecurity school awarded two seven-month contracts in January for access to servers containing eight H200 chips each. The contracts, worth 441,700 yuan and 441,000 yuan, covered fine-tuning AI models and reinforcement-learning training. It also rented access to servers containing eight Nvidia A100 chips and eight A800 chips. The A100 and A800 are banned from export to all Chinese entities, though the H200 is the most advanced of those cited in Northwestern Polytechnical's procurement records. In April, another university institute bought computing services requiring at least 24 A100 chips in a 375,000 yuan contract for structural and fluid-dynamics simulations. The awards went to several little-known Chinese technology suppliers. The records offered scant information about where the processors originated or where the rented servers operated. Under Chinese law, public procurement agencies must verify that suppliers can fulfil orders before announcing winning bidders and signing contracts. The procurement records show a wider market for restricted Nvidia AI chips and computing services at Chinese universities. Shenzhen University bought three H100 processors, another high-end Nvidia AI chip banned by the US, for 769,800 yuan in September. Wuhan University of Technology bought a server containing an H100 chip for 355,000 yuan in June and four A100 chips in a separate 344,000 yuan purchase, the records show. Beihang University, another of the Seven Sons of National Defense universities, bought four A800 processors for 489,000 yuan in April. Beihang has close ties to China's aerospace and defence industries and conducts research for military aviation and space programmes. Two government procurement announcements in July and September named suppliers selected to provide computing services using Nvidia H800 and A800 chips restricted from export to China to the University of Chinese Academy of Sciences. One listed H800 access at 10 yuan per chip-hour. A separate January procurement award named a supplier of six A100 chips worth 484,800 yuan for a Shenzhen-based public institution. Reuters has previously reported that Chinese institutions acquired restricted Nvidia chips embedded in servers made by Super Micro Computer, Dell and Gigabyte through domestic resellers. Reuters has also documented an underground market in China for restricted Nvidia chips sourced from overseas inventories and third-country intermediaries. Last week, Reuters reported that small quantities of H200 chips had reached China through indirect routes while Beijing withheld approval for large-scale imports. (Reporting by Eduardo Baptista; Editing by Jamie Freed)

Other Chinese universities also acquired restricted Nvidia processors.

sources.title: Exclusive-PLA-linked Chinese university bought Nvidia H200 chips despite US blacklist, records show - Centre Daily Times
passages: BEIJING, Nov 11 (Reuters) - A Chinese university with deep ties to the People's Liberation Army bought Nvidia's powerful H200 AI chips last month despite being on a US export blacklist, procurement records show, highlighting gaps in Washington's efforts to curb China's access to advanced technology.
Shenzhen University bought three H100 processors, another high-end Nvidia AI chip banned by the US, for 769,800 yuan in September.
Wuhan University of Technology bought a server containing an H100 chip for 355,000 yuan in June and four A100 chips in a separate 344,000 yuan purchase, the records show.

A Reuters review of 26 Chinese procurement and corporate records from this year found universities and research institutions buying US-restricted Nvidia chips or renting access to Nvidia-powered computing services that use such chips through domestic suppliers.
It also rented access to servers containing eight Nvidia A100 chips and eight A800 chips.
The A100 and A800 are banned from export to all Chinese entities, though the H200 is the most advanced of those cited in Northwestern Polytechnical's procurement records.
The US Commerce Department added the university to its trade blacklist, known as the Entity List, in 2001 over its alleged involvement in missile-proliferation activities and military research.

The January licensing rules also require safeguards to prevent blacklisted entities and military end-users from remotely accessing chips exported under the policy, which covers H200 processors and less advanced models.
Last week, Reuters reported that small quantities of H200 chips had reached China through indirect routes while Beijing withheld approval for large-scale imports.
Northwestern is a member of the "Seven Sons of National Defense" group of Chinese universities under U.S. sanctions and with a history of conducting defence-related research for Beijing.
The chips were purchased for its management school from Shaanxi Bosuan Network Technology rather than directly from Nvidia, the record shows.
The universities named in the records did not respond to requests for comment.

extraction.body: BEIJING, Nov 11 (Reuters) - A Chinese university with deep ties to the People's Liberation Army bought Nvidia's powerful H200 AI chips last month despite being on a US export blacklist, procurement records show, highlighting gaps in Washington's efforts to curb China's access to advanced technology. The findings come as Nvidia and its CEO Jensen Huang face mounting scrutiny in Washington over his lobbying for looser restrictions on sales of AI chips to China, following reports alleging he was targeted by a Chinese spying operation. Huang has argued that continued US sales to China would preserve American technological leadership and keep Chinese customers reliant on US technology. But some US lawmakers say access to Nvidia's most powerful AI chips can speed China's development of AI systems for weapons design, intelligence analysis and military modernisation. Both Democrats and Republicans in Congress have urged stronger controls on China's access to advanced AI chips, such as chip-tracking requirements and greater congressional oversight of exports. Three Republican congressional committee chairmen have requested a briefing with Huang on November 18 over his reported contacts with an alleged Chinese intelligence operative. Northwestern Polytechnical University bought two H200 chips last month for 874,700 yuan ($123,000), according to an October 21 procurement record on its website. Northwestern is a member of the "Seven Sons of National Defense" group of Chinese universities under U.S. sanctions and with a history of conducting defence-related research for Beijing. The chips were purchased for its management school from Shaanxi Bosuan Network Technology rather than directly from Nvidia, the record shows. The H200 is among Nvidia's most capable chips for training and running advanced AI systems and is subject to US export licence approvals, which are normally denied for blacklisted institutions such as Northwestern Polytechnical. Northwestern Polytechnical also bought access this year to H200 chips and other powerful Nvidia AI processors through five contracts for rented computing capacity from Chinese companies, procurement records show. Reuters is reporting the chip purchases and computing contracts for the first time. Northwestern Polytechnical, Nvidia and the US Commerce Department's Bureau of Industry and Security, which oversees export controls, did not respond to requests for comment. Reuters could not determine contact details for Shaanxi Bosuan Network Technology. Based in the northwestern city of Xian, Northwestern Polytechnical conducts research related to military aircraft, missiles and satellites. The US Commerce Department added the university to its trade blacklist, known as the Entity List, in 2001 over its alleged involvement in missile-proliferation activities and military research. It tightened the restrictions in 2019, making licences for exports of controlled US technology to the university subject to a policy of denial in most circumstances. Northwestern Polytechnical's purchases show how Chinese institutions with military ties continue to obtain US AI computing power through domestic suppliers, either by buying chips outright or renting access to servers containing them. A Reuters review of 26 Chinese procurement and corporate records from this year found universities and research institutions buying US-restricted Nvidia chips or renting access to Nvidia-powered computing services that use such chips through domestic suppliers. Several had close links to China's defence industry or military research. The universities named in the records did not respond to requests for comment. US President Donald Trump's administration began allowing some H200 exports to China on a case-by-case basis in January. But that policy did not lift the separate restrictions applying to Entity List organisations such as Northwestern Polytechnical. The January licensing rules also require safeguards to prevent blacklisted entities and military end-users from remotely accessing chips exported under the policy, which covers H200 processors and less advanced models. In addition to the management school's outright purchase of the two H200 chips, procurement records show the university's cybersecurity school awarded two seven-month contracts in January for access to servers containing eight H200 chips each. The contracts, worth 441,700 yuan and 441,000 yuan, covered fine-tuning AI models and reinforcement-learning training. It also rented access to servers containing eight Nvidia A100 chips and eight A800 chips. The A100 and A800 are banned from export to all Chinese entities, though the H200 is the most advanced of those cited in Northwestern Polytechnical's procurement records. In April, another university institute bought computing services requiring at least 24 A100 chips in a 375,000 yuan contract for structural and fluid-dynamics simulations. The awards went to several little-known Chinese technology suppliers. The records offered scant information about where the processors originated or where the rented servers operated. Under Chinese law, public procurement agencies must verify that suppliers can fulfil orders before announcing winning bidders and signing contracts. The procurement records show a wider market for restricted Nvidia AI chips and computing services at Chinese universities. Shenzhen University bought three H100 processors, another high-end Nvidia AI chip banned by the US, for 769,800 yuan in September. Wuhan University of Technology bought a server containing an H100 chip for 355,000 yuan in June and four A100 chips in a separate 344,000 yuan purchase, the records show. Beihang University, another of the Seven Sons of National Defense universities, bought four A800 processors for 489,000 yuan in April. Beihang has close ties to China's aerospace and defence industries and conducts research for military aviation and space programmes. Two government procurement announcements in July and September named suppliers selected to provide computing services using Nvidia H800 and A800 chips restricted from export to China to the University of Chinese Academy of Sciences. One listed H800 access at 10 yuan per chip-hour. A separate January procurement award named a supplier of six A100 chips worth 484,800 yuan for a Shenzhen-based public institution. Reuters has previously reported that Chinese institutions acquired restricted Nvidia chips embedded in servers made by Super Micro Computer, Dell and Gigabyte through domestic resellers. Reuters has also documented an underground market in China for restricted Nvidia chips sourced from overseas inventories and third-country intermediaries. Last week, Reuters reported that small quantities of H200 chips had reached China through indirect routes while Beijing withheld approval for large-scale imports. (Reporting by Eduardo Baptista; Editing by Jamie Freed)

sources.title: Netanyahu says only unity government can guarantee Israel’s security - Arab News
passages: A meeting with Eisenkot on Thursday “only strengthened the conviction that it is essential to form a national unity government” to guarantee Israel’s security, Netanyahu said in a video statement, adding that such a government could “eliminate the Iranian threat once and for all.”
Minutes later, Eisenkot responded by saying Netanyahu “knows he lost the election,” accusing him of playing “tricks” by appealing for a unity government.
Netanyahu’s proposed unity government would be made up of key Jewish parties ranging from the center to the right, while excluding the Arab parties.
Such a plan would see the 48 lawmakers in Eisenkot’s bloc vote in favor of his government, against the 46 Netanyahu backers.
The 26 other members of parliament, from Arab and ultra-Orthodox parties, could abstain, allowing the government to be approved without an absolute majority in the Knesset, which has 120 seats.

“Instead of trying to form a weak and dangerous government... let’s meet in one room, without preconditions, put aside all our disagreements and all the boycotts, and reach agreements for the security and the future of the state,” Netanyahu urged.

“Netanyahu is calling for negotiations while they are already underway; he claims to want unity but... sows division and stokes tensions as if there were no tomorrow,” the former army chief said, adding that “these tricks don’t work on me.”
Another point of contention is the election on Tuesday of the speaker of the Knesset, a post currently held by Amir Ohana, a close Netanyahu ally.
The opposition has put forward Matan Kahana, a former officer in the Israeli army who was fifth on Gadi Eisenkot’s list, to replace him.

extraction.body: JERUSALEM: Israel’s caretaker prime minister Benjamin Netanyahu on Saturday reiterated his calls for a national unity government with his opponent Gadi Eisenkot, who in turn dismissed the appeal as a ruse. The latest exchange comes as Eisenkot is in the midst of negotiations to form a government, after he was tapped for the post of premier on Sunday. A meeting with Eisenkot on Thursday “only strengthened the conviction that it is essential to form a national unity government” to guarantee Israel’s security, Netanyahu said in a video statement, adding that such a government could “eliminate the Iranian threat once and for all.” He said this government would be made up of parties that recognize Israel “as a state for the Jewish people.” It would address security challenges, he added, most notably Iran which he claimed would “not hesitate to use nuclear weapons against us.” The outgoing prime minister warned against Eisenkot’s plan to form a minority government, presented as a “national emergency government.” Such a plan would see the 48 lawmakers in Eisenkot’s bloc vote in favor of his government, against the 46 Netanyahu backers. The 26 other members of parliament, from Arab and ultra-Orthodox parties, could abstain, allowing the government to be approved without an absolute majority in the Knesset, which has 120 seats. “Instead of trying to form a weak and dangerous government... let’s meet in one room, without preconditions, put aside all our disagreements and all the boycotts, and reach agreements for the security and the future of the state,” Netanyahu urged. Minutes later, Eisenkot responded by saying Netanyahu “knows he lost the election,” accusing him of playing “tricks” by appealing for a unity government. “Netanyahu is calling for negotiations while they are already underway; he claims to want unity but... sows division and stokes tensions as if there were no tomorrow,” the former army chief said, adding that “these tricks don’t work on me.” Eisenkot was tapped on Sunday to form a new government within 28 days, with a possible 14-day extension. Negotiations are expected to be difficult, especially as Netanyahu has waged a campaign to discredit Arab-Israeli parties, which gained a record number of seats in the election. Netanyahu’s proposed unity government would be made up of key Jewish parties ranging from the center to the right, while excluding the Arab parties. Eisenkot has indicated he would be open to forming a government with members of Netanyahu’s Likud party, as well as outgoing Finance Minister Bezalel Smotrich’s Religious Zionism, provided their commitment to unity is “sincere.” But a unity government with Netanyahu himself remains unlikely, particularly after Eisenkot denounced his “racist” campaign against Arab parties on Friday. Eisenkot on Saturday reiterated his calls for a “break with the extremists,” notably supporters of far-right minister Itamar Ben Gvir, as a condition for any participation in a government under his leadership. Another point of contention is the election on Tuesday of the speaker of the Knesset, a post currently held by Amir Ohana, a close Netanyahu ally. The opposition has put forward Matan Kahana, a former officer in the Israeli army who was fifth on Gadi Eisenkot’s list, to replace him. “If they (Likud and its allies) are truly seeking a sincere political partnership, as they claim, they must allow the democratic process to unfold normally... and instruct their members of parliament to support the appointment of Matan Kahana,” Eisenkot said.

The outgoing prime minister warned against Eisenkot’s plan to form a minority government, presented as a “national emergency government.”

Such a plan would see the 48 lawmakers in Eisenkot’s bloc vote in favor of his government, against the 46 Netanyahu backers. The 26 other members of parliament, from Arab and ultra-Orthodox parties, could abstain, allowing the government to be approved without an absolute majority in the Knesset, which has 120 seats.

“Instead of trying to form a weak and dangerous government... let’s meet in one room, without preconditions, put aside all our disagreements and all the boycotts, and reach agreements for the security and the future of the state,” Netanyahu urged.
Minutes later, Eisenkot responded by saying Netanyahu “knows he lost the election,” accusing him of playing “tricks” by appealing for a unity government.

“Netanyahu is calling for negotiations while they are already underway; he claims to want unity but... sows division and stokes tensions as if there were no tomorrow,” the former army chief said, adding that “these tricks don’t work on me.”
Eisenkot was tapped on Sunday to form a new government within 28 days, with a possible 14-day extension.
Negotiations are expected to be difficult, especially as Netanyahu has waged a campaign to discredit Arab-Israeli parties, which gained a record number of seats in the election.
Netanyahu’s proposed unity government would be made up of key Jewish parties ranging from the center to the right, while excluding the Arab parties.

Eisenkot has indicated he would be open to forming a government with members of Netanyahu’s Likud party, as well as outgoing Finance Minister Bezalel Smotrich’s Religious Zionism, provided their commitment to unity is “sincere.”
But a unity government with Netanyahu himself remains unlikely, particularly after Eisenkot denounced his “racist” campaign against Arab parties on Friday.

Eisenkot on Saturday reiterated his calls for a “break with the extremists,” notably supporters of far-right minister Itamar Ben Gvir, as a condition for any participation in a government under his leadership.

Another point of contention is the election on Tuesday of the speaker of the Knesset, a post currently held by Amir Ohana, a close Netanyahu ally. The opposition has put forward Matan Kahana, a former officer in the Israeli army who was fifth on Gadi Eisenkot’s list, to replace him.

“If they (Likud and its allies) are truly seeking a sincere political partnership, as they claim, they must allow the democratic process to unfold normally... and instruct their members of parliament to support the appointment of Matan Kahana,” Eisenkot said.

Israeli caretaker Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu renewed his call for a national unity government with Gadi Eisenkot, saying a meeting with Eisenkot on Thursday “only strengthened the conviction that it is essential to form a national unity government”. Netanyahu argued that such a government could “eliminate the Iranian threat once and for all”, claiming Tehran would “not hesitate to use nuclear weapons against us”.

Netanyahu said he urged Eisenkot to “Let’s meet in one room, without preconditions,” and he framed the talks as a way to address Israel’s security challenges. Eisenkot dismissed Netanyahu’s appeal as a ploy, saying Netanyahu “knows he lost the election” and adding, “These tricks don’t work on me.”
Netanyahu proposed rotation is discussed by his bloc, without preconditions.

Neither side won a majority in the October 27 election, with Netanyahu’s right-wing and religious bloc taking 53 seats in the 120-seat Knesset and Eisenkot’s four-party bloc taking 48 seats. Arab-led parties won a record 19 seats, and President Isaac Herzog tasked Eisenkot with forming a government after 67 lawmakers, including those from Arab-led parties, endorsed him. Netanyahu’s warning against Eisenkot’s plan for a minority “national emergency government” said the 48 lawmakers in Eisenkot’s bloc would vote in favour against the 46 Netanyahu backers while the 26 other members could abstain.

Eisenkot was tapped to form a government within 28 days, with a possible 14-day extension, and Netanyahu’s unity proposal would exclude Arab parties. Eisenkot “knows he lost the election”, and Eisenkot accused Netanyahu of playing “tricks” by appealing for a unity government.

The standoff over unity has carried into the Knesset, where the parliament will elect its speaker on Tuesday, with Amir Ohana holding the post and the opposition putting forward Matan Kahana. Eisenkot challenged Likud and Religious Zionism to support the appointment of Matan Kahana, and Eisenkot said, “If they (Likud and its allies) are truly seeking a sincere political partnership”. Eisenkot ruled out including Arab-led parties in his government, while Netanyahu’s version would include Jewish parties from the centre and the right and exclude Arab parties.

Eisenkot said he could work with members of Netanyahu’s Likud party and with Bezalel Smotrich’s Religious Zionism if their commitment to unity is “sincere”, but he insisted on a “break with the extremists”. Netanyahu warned that such a government would lead to Israel’s “collapse”, while Eisenkot’s bloc could approve his minority plan without an absolute majority in the Knesset.

extraction.body: For feedback, please contact english@ilsole24ore.com Donald Trump will discuss Iran, but not Ukraine, with his counterparts Xi Jinping and Vladimir Putin during the trilateral talks scheduled for next Thursday on the sidelines of the APEC summit in Shenzhen, China. This is according to the White House. The leaders of the US, China and Russia, in their first-ever trilateral meeting, may also discuss their respective nuclear arsenals, according to a senior US official. The latest nuclear arms control treaty between Washington and Moscow expired in February, removing, for the first time in over half a century, the limits on the world’s two largest nuclear arsenals. When the agreement, known as ‘New Start’, expired, Trump rejected the Russian proposal to extend it by a year, calling instead for a “new, improved and modernised” deal that would also include China. The trilateral meeting is intended to be a “start to what we hope will be a conversation” on nuclear disarmament, “capable of leading to productive developments in the future”, the official added, noting that no announcements of agreements are expected. Beijing’s arsenal, which according to Pentagon estimates comprises over 600 warheads, is far smaller than that of the US and Russia, each of which possesses more than 5,000. Given this stark disparity, China has shown little interest in opening discussions on the issue, instead calling for a reduction in the number of warheads held by Washington and Moscow. The Trump administration recognises that, for Beijing, the issue may be complex: the official, however, described next week’s meeting as an opportunity for China to ‘take its place at the big table’ on a matter of international significance. Yashar leader Gadi Eisenkot dismisses Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu’s offer to negotiate a national unity government, calling it “yet another propaganda ploy”, and points out that the Likud and Yashar negotiating teams have already arranged a meeting for tomorrow. “He claims to want unity, but then he trivialises an institutional ceremony in the Knesset, sowing division and inciting hatred as if there were no tomorrow,” says Eisenkot, according to the Times of Israel. “Nice try, but these tricks don’t work on me. And they don’t work on the citizens of Israel either.” The Houthis claim that forces from the Saudi-led coalition have carried out 72 air strikes in the last 24 hours in the Yemeni provinces of Sa’ada, Ta’izz, Lahij and al-Jawf. This was reported by the Al Jazeera satellite network’s website, which added: this brings the total number of air and missile strikes to 5,020 since fighting resumed in Yemen this summer, as military spokesman Yahya Saree wrote on X. (Foto AP/Vahid Salemi) APN The head of Hamas’s political bureau, Khalil al-Hayya, has called for “urgent action” to repair Gaza’s sewerage network following the floods and to improve the rainwater drainage system. This was reported on the website of the satellite news channel Al Jazeera. “What Gaza is experiencing,” he explained, “is no longer an emergency humanitarian crisis nor a natural consequence of the war, but a complex reality in which policies of starvation, systematic destruction and the deliberate restriction of aid deliveries are intertwined.” Al-Hayya called for “unhindered” access for humanitarian organisations and for larger quantities of food and fuel to be allowed into the Gaza Strip. Heavy rains in Gaza have destroyed tens of thousands of tents. Israeli restrictions on aid – as Al Jazeera points out – have hampered attempts to rebuild the Strip’s devastated infrastructure. Benyamin Netanyahu is not giving up and continues to call for a government of national unity as the only solution to “guarantee Israel’s security”. This is stated in a declaration issued by the acting Prime Minister following the Jewish Sabbath. In this declaration, Netanyahu also reaffirms his commitment to resuming the war to eliminate “the Iranian threat once and for all”. The message is addressed to the nation, but indirectly also to the leader of the opposition, Gadi Eisenkot, who was tasked following the recent elections with attempting to form a new government from which he aims to exclude ‘Bibi’. An attack carried out by an Israeli drone has killed two Palestinians in Jabaliya, on the northern outskirts of Gaza City, according to hospital officials. Several other people were injured, although the exact number has not been specified. The Israeli army said it had targeted two Hamas militants. Today’s attack comes against a backdrop of ongoing violence in Gaza, where more than 1,600 Palestinians have lost their lives since a ceasefire was reached over a year ago. Meanwhile, Iranian state television reported that three oil tankers had struck naval mines and caught fire near the Strait of Hormuz. The Iranian authorities have warned that vessels passing through the strait without Iran’s approval will face a similar fate. The European Union has called on Israel to grant urgent access to Gaza for humanitarian organisations, in order to help the victims of the devastating floods that have hit the Strip. “We urge Israel to allow immediate and unhindered access, as well as the sustained distribution of humanitarian aid and support for a large-scale initial recovery, and to reopen all Gaza border crossings,” a statement said. Last week, COGAT announced that it had stepped up its efforts to improve sanitation and hygiene conditions in Gaza ahead of the heavy rains, in coordination with international organisations. Israel, for its part, responded that allegations that COGAT was not allowing sufficient supplies to enter “divert attention from Hamas’s responsibilities”. The Revolutionary Guards, the Iranian Pasdaran, claim to have shot down a US drone flying over the island of Qeshm. Overnight, according to reports from the Iranian broadcaster IRIB, as relayed by the satellite TV channel Al Jazeera, “an American MQ-1 Predator drone” was “intercepted and destroyed” using a “new air defence system”. For the Pasdaran, this is the seventeenth MQ-1 drone to have been shot down. The island of Qeshm – situated near the Strait of Hormuz, not far from the port city of Bandar Abbas, off the southern coast of the Islamic Republic – has been the target of limited raids by US forces in recent days. More oil, with prices beginning to stabilise. Not only has the supply of crude oil recovered – to the point where it is once again exceeding demand thanks to the resumption of supplies from the Persian Gulf, according to the International Energy Agency – but, in addition to the price per barrel, all the ‘incidental costs’ that had soared to unprecedented levels during the war are now falling sharply: from the differentials on many grades of crude to sea freight rates, which have more than halved on the main routes within the space of a couple of weeks. The charter rates for oil tankers remain very high: after all, they had soared to seven or eight times their previous levels as a result of the war in the Middle East, which disrupted logistics with global repercussions. But the turnaround is clear and truly remarkable, especially given that tensions in the Persian Gulf region have not abated. The US might refrain from launching further attacks against Iran if Tehran and the Houthis in Yemen do not carry out any further provocations. This is what US President Donald Trump is said to have confided to his closest advisers in recent days, according to three informed sources cited by Reuters. The news has been picked up by several international media outlets, including Sky News Arabia and Al-Arabiya. After weeks of threats of military escalation and overtures towards a possible end to hostilities, Trump is reportedly considering a pause. The possibility is said to have emerged during a number of meetings with national security advisers and following a series of intelligence briefings. The White House’s assessment is also reportedly influenced by requests from allies in the region, who are opposed to a return to full-scale war. “I could end the war immediately, but at the request of the nations I am trying to protect, we are taking a slightly longer, slightly more civilised path,” Trump said in an interview on Thursday. A child from Gaza underwent a complex operation for advanced bilateral retinoblastoma: the operation was carried out at the Meyer Children’s Hospital in Florence in collaboration with the Siena University Hospital. Following the operation in Florence, the young patient was transferred to Siena to complete his hospital stay and undergo further checks, after which he was discharged. In a joint statement, AOU Meyer IRCCS and AOU Senese explain that this was an “extremely delicate combined neurosurgical and ophthalmological procedure to address one of the most serious complications of retinoblastoma”. The operation involved the ophthalmology team from the Retinoblastoma Reference Centre at AOU Senese, alongside the neurosurgery and ophthalmology departments at the AOU Meyer Children’s Hospital, joining forces in a procedure which, according to the doctors, could open up new prospects for the child, who had previously undergone numerous treatments, including systemic chemotherapy, intra-arterial and intravitreal chemotherapy, and focal therapies, in an attempt to control a particularly aggressive form of cancer. And despite the treatment, at his last check-up, he was found to have “spread of the disease along the optic nerve almost as far as the chiasm, an extremely serious condition requiring a life-saving, specialist assessment and a surgical approach of exceptional difficulty never before performed in Tuscany”. “The initial outcome was positive,” the statement reads, “and represents an important opportunity for the child, in a clinical context that requires careful monitoring and further assessments over time.” The President of Tuscany, Eugenio Giani, emphasises that “once again, Tuscany’s public health service has demonstrated its high level of specialisation, combined with its commitment to international medical rescue operations”. The Regional Councillor for Health, Monia Monni, adds: “The young patient arrived in Italia as part of a Medevac mission to evacuate people from crisis zones. I was also on the plane that brought him out of the occupied Gaza Strip. These journeys are always difficult, but wonderful because of the hope they bring.” Since the start of the conflict in the Persian Gulf on 28 February, inflation in Italia has risen by 4.4 per cent, with peaks of +5.4 per cent in Como, +5.1 per cent in Siena and Lucca, and +4.6 per cent in Florence, Trieste, Verona, Vicenza and Syracuse. Donald Trump will discuss Iran, but not Ukraine, with his counterparts Xi Jinping and Vladimir Putin during the trilateral talks scheduled for next Thursday on the sidelines of the APEC summit in Shenzhen, China. This is according to the White House.

The leaders of the US, China and Russia, in their first-ever trilateral meeting, may also discuss their respective nuclear arsenals, according to a senior US official. The latest nuclear arms control treaty between Washington and Moscow expired in February, removing, for the first time in over half a century, the limits on the world’s two largest nuclear arsenals. When the agreement, known as ‘New Start’, expired, Trump rejected the Russian proposal to extend it by a year, calling instead for a “new, improved and modernised” deal that would also include China. The trilateral meeting is intended to be a “start to what we hope will be a conversation” on nuclear disarmament, “capable of leading to productive developments in the future”, the official added, noting that no announcements of agreements are expected. Beijing’s arsenal, which according to Pentagon estimates comprises over 600 warheads, is far smaller than that of the US and Russia, each of which possesses more than 5,000. Given this stark disparity, China has shown little interest in opening discussions on the issue, instead calling for a reduction in the number of warheads held by Washington and Moscow. The Trump administration recognises that, for Beijing, the issue may be complex: the official, however, described next week’s meeting as an opportunity for China to ‘take its place at the big table’ on a matter of international significance.

“What Gaza is experiencing,” he explained, “is no longer an emergency humanitarian crisis nor a natural consequence of the war, but a complex reality in which policies of starvation, systematic destruction and the deliberate restriction of aid deliveries are intertwined.” Al-Hayya called for “unhindered” access for humanitarian organisations and for larger quantities of food and fuel to be allowed into the Gaza Strip. Heavy rains in Gaza have destroyed tens of thousands of tents. Israeli restrictions on aid – as Al Jazeera points out – have hampered attempts to rebuild the Strip’s devastated infrastructure.

Benyamin Netanyahu is not giving up and continues to call for a government of national unity as the only solution to “guarantee Israel’s security”. This is stated in a declaration issued by the acting Prime Minister following the Jewish Sabbath. In this declaration, Netanyahu also reaffirms his commitment to resuming the war to eliminate “the Iranian threat once and for all”. The message is addressed to the nation, but indirectly also to the leader of the opposition, Gadi Eisenkot, who was tasked following the recent elections with attempting to form a new government from which he aims to exclude ‘Bibi’.

An attack carried out by an Israeli drone has killed two Palestinians in Jabaliya, on the northern outskirts of Gaza City, according to hospital officials. Today’s attack comes against a backdrop of ongoing violence in Gaza, where more than 1,600 Palestinians have lost their lives since a ceasefire was reached over a year ago.

Meanwhile, Iranian state television reported that three oil tankers had struck naval mines and caught fire near the Strait of Hormuz. The Iranian authorities have warned that vessels passing through the strait without Iran’s approval will face a similar fate.
The European Union has called on Israel to grant urgent access to Gaza for humanitarian organisations, in order to help the victims of the devastating floods that have hit the Strip.

“We urge Israel to allow immediate and unhindered access, as well as the sustained distribution of humanitarian aid and support for a large-scale initial recovery, and to reopen all Gaza border crossings,” a statement said.

Last week, COGAT announced that it had stepped up its efforts to improve sanitation and hygiene conditions in Gaza ahead of the heavy rains, in coordination with international organisations. Israel, for its part, responded that allegations that COGAT was not allowing sufficient supplies to enter “divert attention from Hamas’s responsibilities”.

The Revolutionary Guards, the Iranian Pasdaran, claim to have shot down a US drone flying over the island of Qeshm. Overnight, according to reports from the Iranian broadcaster IRIB, as relayed by the satellite TV channel Al Jazeera, “an American MQ-1 Predator drone” was “intercepted and destroyed” using a “new air defence system”. For the Pasdaran, this is the seventeenth MQ-1 drone to have been shot down. The island of Qeshm – situated near the Strait of Hormuz, not far from the port city of Bandar Abbas, off the southern coast of the Islamic Republic – has been the target of limited raids by US forces in recent days.

More oil, with prices beginning to stabilise.
