The charter rates for oil tankers remain very high: after all, they had soared to seven or eight times their previous levels as a result of the war in the Middle East, which disrupted logistics with global repercussions. But the turnaround is clear and truly remarkable, especially given that tensions in the Persian Gulf region have not abated.

The US might refrain from launching further attacks against Iran if Tehran and the Houthis in Yemen do not carry out any further provocations. This is what US President Donald Trump is said to have confided to his closest advisers in recent days, according to three informed sources cited by Reuters. The news has been picked up by several international media outlets, including Sky News Arabia and Al-Arabiya. After weeks of threats of military escalation and overtures towards a possible end to hostilities, Trump is reportedly considering a pause. The possibility is said to have emerged during a number of meetings with national security advisers and following a series of intelligence briefings. The White House’s assessment is also reportedly influenced by requests from allies in the region, who are opposed to a return to full-scale war. “I could end the war immediately, but at the request of the nations I am trying to protect, we are taking a slightly longer, slightly more civilised path,” Trump said in an interview on Thursday.

Following the operation in Florence, the young patient was transferred to Siena to complete his hospital stay and undergo further checks, after which he was discharged.

In a joint statement, AOU Meyer IRCCS and AOU Senese explain that this was an “extremely delicate combined neurosurgical and ophthalmological procedure to address one of the most serious complications of retinoblastoma”. passages: Israeli caretaker Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu has renewed his call for a national unity government with his rival, Gadi Eisenkot, saying only such a government can guarantee Israel’s security.

Under Eisenkot’s plan for a minority “national emergency government”, his bloc’s 48 lawmakers would vote in favour against the 46 Netanyahu supporters, while the 26 lawmakers from Arab and ultra-Orthodox parties could abstain.
It would allow his government to be approved without an absolute majority in the Knesset.
President Isaac Herzog last week tasked Eisenkot with forming a government, after 67 lawmakers, including those from Arab-led parties, endorsed him, while 46 backed Netanyahu.

Eisenkot has said he could work with members of Netanyahu’s Likud party and with Bezalel Smotrich’s Religious Zionism if their commitment to unity is “sincere”, but he insisted on a “break with the extremists”, notably supporters of far-right minister Itamar Ben-Gvir.
A former army chief, Eisenkot said Netanyahu “knows he lost the election”.
“Netanyahu is calling for negotiations while they are already underway,” he said.
Netanyahu’s version would include Jewish parties from the centre and the right and exclude Arab parties .
On Friday, Eisenkot called Netanyahu’s campaign against them “racist” .
The Knesset will elect its speaker on Tuesday.
The post is currently held by Netanyahu ally Amir Ohana, and the opposition has put forward Matan Kahana, a former military officer, in his place.

extraction.body: Eisenkot, in charge of forming a government, dismisses the appeal as ‘tricks’ as talks and a Knesset speaker vote loom. Israeli caretaker Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu has renewed his call for a national unity government with his rival, Gadi Eisenkot, saying only such a government can guarantee Israel’s security. In a video statement on Saturday, Netanyahu said a meeting with Eisenkot on Thursday “only strengthened the conviction that it is essential to form a national unity government”. The prime minister said such a government could “eliminate the Iranian threat once and for all”, claiming Tehran would “not hesitate to use nuclear weapons against us”. “Let’s meet in one room, without preconditions,” he said. Within minutes, however, Eisenkot dismissed the appeal as a ploy. A former army chief, Eisenkot said Netanyahu “knows he lost the election”. “Netanyahu is calling for negotiations while they are already underway,” he said. “These tricks don’t work on me.” Neither side won a majority in the October 27 election. Netanyahu’s right-wing and religious bloc took 53 seats in the 120-seat Knesset, Eisenkot’s four-party bloc got 48 seats, and Arab-led parties won a record 19. President Isaac Herzog last week tasked Eisenkot with forming a government, after 67 lawmakers, including those from Arab-led parties, endorsed him, while 46 backed Netanyahu. Eisenkot has 28 days, with a possible 14-day extension. He has ruled out including Arab-led parties in his government. Under Eisenkot’s plan for a minority “national emergency government”, his bloc’s 48 lawmakers would vote in favour against the 46 Netanyahu supporters, while the 26 lawmakers from Arab and ultra-Orthodox parties could abstain. It would allow his government to be approved without an absolute majority in the Knesset. Netanyahu has warned that such a government would lead to Israel’s “collapse”. Netanyahu’s version would include Jewish parties from the centre and the right and exclude Arab parties . He and his allies have made unsubstantiated claims that Arab-led parties “stole” the election. On Friday, Eisenkot called Netanyahu’s campaign against them “racist” . Eisenkot has said he could work with members of Netanyahu’s Likud party and with Bezalel Smotrich’s Religious Zionism if their commitment to unity is “sincere”, but he insisted on a “break with the extremists”, notably supporters of far-right minister Itamar Ben-Gvir. The Knesset will elect its speaker on Tuesday. The post is currently held by Netanyahu ally Amir Ohana, and the opposition has put forward Matan Kahana, a former military officer, in his place.

Minutes later, Eisenkot responded by saying Netanyahu “knows he lost the election,” accusing him of playing “tricks” by appealing for a unity government.
Netanyahu’s proposed unity government would be made up of key Jewish parties ranging from the center to the right, while excluding the Arab parties.
Such a plan would see the 48 lawmakers in Eisenkot’s bloc vote in favor of his government, against the 46 Netanyahu backers.
The 26 other members of parliament, from Arab and ultra-Orthodox parties, could abstain, allowing the government to be approved without an absolute majority in the Knesset, which has 120 seats.

“Instead of trying to form a weak and dangerous government... let’s meet in one room, without preconditions, put aside all our disagreements and all the boycotts, and reach agreements for the security and the future of the state,” Netanyahu urged.

“Netanyahu is calling for negotiations while they are already underway; he claims to want unity but... sows division and stokes tensions as if there were no tomorrow,” the former army chief said, adding that “these tricks don’t work on me.”
Another point of contention is the election on Tuesday of the speaker of the Knesset, a post currently held by Amir Ohana, a close Netanyahu ally.
The opposition has put forward Matan Kahana, a former officer in the Israeli army who was fifth on Gadi Eisenkot’s list, to replace him.

extraction.body: JERUSALEM: Israel’s caretaker prime minister Benjamin Netanyahu on Saturday reiterated his calls for a national unity government with his opponent Gadi Eisenkot, who in turn dismissed the appeal as a ruse. The latest exchange comes as Eisenkot is in the midst of negotiations to form a government, after he was tapped for the post of premier on Sunday. A meeting with Eisenkot on Thursday “only strengthened the conviction that it is essential to form a national unity government” to guarantee Israel’s security, Netanyahu said in a video statement, adding that such a government could “eliminate the Iranian threat once and for all.” He said this government would be made up of parties that recognize Israel “as a state for the Jewish people.” It would address security challenges, he added, most notably Iran which he claimed would “not hesitate to use nuclear weapons against us.” The outgoing prime minister warned against Eisenkot’s plan to form a minority government, presented as a “national emergency government.” Such a plan would see the 48 lawmakers in Eisenkot’s bloc vote in favor of his government, against the 46 Netanyahu backers. The 26 other members of parliament, from Arab and ultra-Orthodox parties, could abstain, allowing the government to be approved without an absolute majority in the Knesset, which has 120 seats. “Instead of trying to form a weak and dangerous government... let’s meet in one room, without preconditions, put aside all our disagreements and all the boycotts, and reach agreements for the security and the future of the state,” Netanyahu urged. Minutes later, Eisenkot responded by saying Netanyahu “knows he lost the election,” accusing him of playing “tricks” by appealing for a unity government. “Netanyahu is calling for negotiations while they are already underway; he claims to want unity but... sows division and stokes tensions as if there were no tomorrow,” the former army chief said, adding that “these tricks don’t work on me.” Eisenkot was tapped on Sunday to form a new government within 28 days, with a possible 14-day extension. Negotiations are expected to be difficult, especially as Netanyahu has waged a campaign to discredit Arab-Israeli parties, which gained a record number of seats in the election. Netanyahu’s proposed unity government would be made up of key Jewish parties ranging from the center to the right, while excluding the Arab parties. Eisenkot has indicated he would be open to forming a government with members of Netanyahu’s Likud party, as well as outgoing Finance Minister Bezalel Smotrich’s Religious Zionism, provided their commitment to unity is “sincere.” But a unity government with Netanyahu himself remains unlikely, particularly after Eisenkot denounced his “racist” campaign against Arab parties on Friday. Eisenkot on Saturday reiterated his calls for a “break with the extremists,” notably supporters of far-right minister Itamar Ben Gvir, as a condition for any participation in a government under his leadership. Another point of contention is the election on Tuesday of the speaker of the Knesset, a post currently held by Amir Ohana, a close Netanyahu ally. The opposition has put forward Matan Kahana, a former officer in the Israeli army who was fifth on Gadi Eisenkot’s list, to replace him. “If they (Likud and its allies) are truly seeking a sincere political partnership, as they claim, they must allow the democratic process to unfold normally... and instruct their members of parliament to support the appointment of Matan Kahana,” Eisenkot said.

Netanyahu’s proposed unity government would be made up of key Jewish parties ranging from the center to the right, while excluding the Arab parties.

Eisenkot has indicated he would be open to forming a government with members of Netanyahu’s Likud party, as well as outgoing Finance Minister Bezalel Smotrich’s Religious Zionism, provided their commitment to unity is “sincere.”
But a unity government with Netanyahu himself remains unlikely, particularly after Eisenkot denounced his “racist” campaign against Arab parties on Friday.

Eisenkot on Saturday reiterated his calls for a “break with the extremists,” notably supporters of far-right minister Itamar Ben Gvir, as a condition for any participation in a government under his leadership.

Another point of contention is the election on Tuesday of the speaker of the Knesset, a post currently held by Amir Ohana, a close Netanyahu ally. The opposition has put forward Matan Kahana, a former officer in the Israeli army who was fifth on Gadi Eisenkot’s list, to replace him.

“If they (Likud and its allies) are truly seeking a sincere political partnership, as they claim, they must allow the democratic process to unfold normally... and instruct their members of parliament to support the appointment of Matan Kahana,” Eisenkot said.

Israeli caretaker Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu renewed his call for a national unity government with Gadi Eisenkot, saying a meeting with Eisenkot on Thursday “only strengthened the conviction that it is essential to form a national unity government”. Netanyahu argued that such a government could “eliminate the Iranian threat once and for all”, claiming Tehran would “not hesitate to use nuclear weapons against us”.

Netanyahu said he urged Eisenkot to “Let’s meet in one room, without preconditions,” and he framed the talks as a way to address Israel’s security challenges. Eisenkot dismissed Netanyahu’s appeal as a ploy, saying Netanyahu “knows he lost the election” and adding, “These tricks don’t work on me.”
Netanyahu proposed rotation is discussed by his bloc, without preconditions.

Neither side won a majority in the October 27 election, with Netanyahu’s right-wing and religious bloc taking 53 seats in the 120-seat Knesset and Eisenkot’s four-party bloc taking 48 seats. Arab-led parties won a record 19 seats, and President Isaac Herzog tasked Eisenkot with forming a government after 67 lawmakers, including those from Arab-led parties, endorsed him. Netanyahu’s warning against Eisenkot’s plan for a minority “national emergency government” said the 48 lawmakers in Eisenkot’s bloc would vote in favour against the 46 Netanyahu backers while the 26 other members could abstain.

Eisenkot was tapped to form a government within 28 days, with a possible 14-day extension, and Netanyahu’s unity proposal would exclude Arab parties. Eisenkot “knows he lost the election”, and Eisenkot accused Netanyahu of playing “tricks” by appealing for a unity government.

The standoff over unity has carried into the Knesset, where the parliament will elect its speaker on Tuesday, with Amir Ohana holding the post and the opposition putting forward Matan Kahana. Eisenkot challenged Likud and Religious Zionism to support the appointment of Matan Kahana, and Eisenkot said, “If they (Likud and its allies) are truly seeking a sincere political partnership”. Eisenkot ruled out including Arab-led parties in his government, while Netanyahu’s version would include Jewish parties from the centre and the right and exclude Arab parties.

Eisenkot said he could work with members of Netanyahu’s Likud party and with Bezalel Smotrich’s Religious Zionism if their commitment to unity is “sincere”, but he insisted on a “break with the extremists”. extraction.body: For feedback, please contact english@ilsole24ore.com Donald Trump will discuss Iran, but not Ukraine, with his counterparts Xi Jinping and Vladimir Putin during the trilateral talks scheduled for next Thursday on the sidelines of the APEC summit in Shenzhen, China. This is according to the White House. The leaders of the US, China and Russia, in their first-ever trilateral meeting, may also discuss their respective nuclear arsenals, according to a senior US official. The latest nuclear arms control treaty between Washington and Moscow expired in February, removing, for the first time in over half a century, the limits on the world’s two largest nuclear arsenals. When the agreement, known as ‘New Start’, expired, Trump rejected the Russian proposal to extend it by a year, calling instead for a “new, improved and modernised” deal that would also include China. The trilateral meeting is intended to be a “start to what we hope will be a conversation” on nuclear disarmament, “capable of leading to productive developments in the future”, the official added, noting that no announcements of agreements are expected. Beijing’s arsenal, which according to Pentagon estimates comprises over 600 warheads, is far smaller than that of the US and Russia, each of which possesses more than 5,000. Given this stark disparity, China has shown little interest in opening discussions on the issue, instead calling for a reduction in the number of warheads held by Washington and Moscow. The Trump administration recognises that, for Beijing, the issue may be complex: the official, however, described next week’s meeting as an opportunity for China to ‘take its place at the big table’ on a matter of international significance. Yashar leader Gadi Eisenkot dismisses Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu’s offer to negotiate a national unity government, calling it “yet another propaganda ploy”, and points out that the Likud and Yashar negotiating teams have already arranged a meeting for tomorrow. “He claims to want unity, but then he trivialises an institutional ceremony in the Knesset, sowing division and inciting hatred as if there were no tomorrow,” says Eisenkot, according to the Times of Israel. “Nice try, but these tricks don’t work on me. And they don’t work on the citizens of Israel either.” The Houthis claim that forces from the Saudi-led coalition have carried out 72 air strikes in the last 24 hours in the Yemeni provinces of Sa’ada, Ta’izz, Lahij and al-Jawf. This was reported by the Al Jazeera satellite network’s website, which added: this brings the total number of air and missile strikes to 5,020 since fighting resumed in Yemen this summer, as military spokesman Yahya Saree wrote on X. (Foto AP/Vahid Salemi) APN The head of Hamas’s political bureau, Khalil al-Hayya, has called for “urgent action” to repair Gaza’s sewerage network following the floods and to improve the rainwater drainage system. This was reported on the website of the satellite news channel Al Jazeera. “What Gaza is experiencing,” he explained, “is no longer an emergency humanitarian crisis nor a natural consequence of the war, but a complex reality in which policies of starvation, systematic destruction and the deliberate restriction of aid deliveries are intertwined.” Al-Hayya called for “unhindered” access for humanitarian organisations and for larger quantities of food and fuel to be allowed into the Gaza Strip. Heavy rains in Gaza have destroyed tens of thousands of tents. Israeli restrictions on aid – as Al Jazeera points out – have hampered attempts to rebuild the Strip’s devastated infrastructure. Benyamin Netanyahu is not giving up and continues to call for a government of national unity as the only solution to “guarantee Israel’s security”. This is stated in a declaration issued by the acting Prime Minister following the Jewish Sabbath. In this declaration, Netanyahu also reaffirms his commitment to resuming the war to eliminate “the Iranian threat once and for all”. The message is addressed to the nation, but indirectly also to the leader of the opposition, Gadi Eisenkot, who was tasked following the recent elections with attempting to form a new government from which he aims to exclude ‘Bibi’. An attack carried out by an Israeli drone has killed two Palestinians in Jabaliya, on the northern outskirts of Gaza City, according to hospital officials. Several other people were injured, although the exact number has not been specified. The Israeli army said it had targeted two Hamas militants. Today’s attack comes against a backdrop of ongoing violence in Gaza, where more than 1,600 Palestinians have lost their lives since a ceasefire was reached over a year ago. Meanwhile, Iranian state television reported that three oil tankers had struck naval mines and caught fire near the Strait of Hormuz. The Iranian authorities have warned that vessels passing through the strait without Iran’s approval will face a similar fate. The European Union has called on Israel to grant urgent access to Gaza for humanitarian organisations, in order to help the victims of the devastating floods that have hit the Strip. “We urge Israel to allow immediate and unhindered access, as well as the sustained distribution of humanitarian aid and support for a large-scale initial recovery, and to reopen all Gaza border crossings,” a statement said. Last week, COGAT announced that it had stepped up its efforts to improve sanitation and hygiene conditions in Gaza ahead of the heavy rains, in coordination with international organisations. Israel, for its part, responded that allegations that COGAT was not allowing sufficient supplies to enter “divert attention from Hamas’s responsibilities”. The Revolutionary Guards, the Iranian Pasdaran, claim to have shot down a US drone flying over the island of Qeshm. Overnight, according to reports from the Iranian broadcaster IRIB, as relayed by the satellite TV channel Al Jazeera, “an American MQ-1 Predator drone” was “intercepted and destroyed” using a “new air defence system”. For the Pasdaran, this is the seventeenth MQ-1 drone to have been shot down. The island of Qeshm – situated near the Strait of Hormuz, not far from the port city of Bandar Abbas, off the southern coast of the Islamic Republic – has been the target of limited raids by US forces in recent days. More oil, with prices beginning to stabilise. Not only has the supply of crude oil recovered – to the point where it is once again exceeding demand thanks to the resumption of supplies from the Persian Gulf, according to the International Energy Agency – but, in addition to the price per barrel, all the ‘incidental costs’ that had soared to unprecedented levels during the war are now falling sharply: from the differentials on many grades of crude to sea freight rates, which have more than halved on the main routes within the space of a couple of weeks. The charter rates for oil tankers remain very high: after all, they had soared to seven or eight times their previous levels as a result of the war in the Middle East, which disrupted logistics with global repercussions. But the turnaround is clear and truly remarkable, especially given that tensions in the Persian Gulf region have not abated. The US might refrain from launching further attacks against Iran if Tehran and the Houthis in Yemen do not carry out any further provocations. This is what US President Donald Trump is said to have confided to his closest advisers in recent days, according to three informed sources cited by Reuters. The news has been picked up by several international media outlets, including Sky News Arabia and Al-Arabiya. After weeks of threats of military escalation and overtures towards a possible end to hostilities, Trump is reportedly considering a pause. The possibility is said to have emerged during a number of meetings with national security advisers and following a series of intelligence briefings. The White House’s assessment is also reportedly influenced by requests from allies in the region, who are opposed to a return to full-scale war. “I could end the war immediately, but at the request of the nations I am trying to protect, we are taking a slightly longer, slightly more civilised path,” Trump said in an interview on Thursday. A child from Gaza underwent a complex operation for advanced bilateral retinoblastoma: the operation was carried out at the Meyer Children’s Hospital in Florence in collaboration with the Siena University Hospital. Following the operation in Florence, the young patient was transferred to Siena to complete his hospital stay and undergo further checks, after which he was discharged. In a joint statement, AOU Meyer IRCCS and AOU Senese explain that this was an “extremely delicate combined neurosurgical and ophthalmological procedure to address one of the most serious complications of retinoblastoma”. The operation involved the ophthalmology team from the Retinoblastoma Reference Centre at AOU Senese, alongside the neurosurgery and ophthalmology departments at the AOU Meyer Children’s Hospital, joining forces in a procedure which, according to the doctors, could open up new prospects for the child, who had previously undergone numerous treatments, including systemic chemotherapy, intra-arterial and intravitreal chemotherapy, and focal therapies, in an attempt to control a particularly aggressive form of cancer. And despite the treatment, at his last check-up, he was found to have “spread of the disease along the optic nerve almost as far as the chiasm, an extremely serious condition requiring a life-saving, specialist assessment and a surgical approach of exceptional difficulty never before performed in Tuscany”. “The initial outcome was positive,” the statement reads, “and represents an important opportunity for the child, in a clinical context that requires careful monitoring and further assessments over time.” The President of Tuscany, Eugenio Giani, emphasises that “once again, Tuscany’s public health service has demonstrated its high level of specialisation, combined with its commitment to international medical rescue operations”. The Regional Councillor for Health, Monia Monni, adds: “The young patient arrived in Italia as part of a Medevac mission to evacuate people from crisis zones. I was also on the plane that brought him out of the occupied Gaza Strip. These journeys are always difficult, but wonderful because of the hope they bring.” Since the start of the conflict in the Persian Gulf on 28 February, inflation in Italia has risen by 4.4 per cent, with peaks of +5.4 per cent in Como, +5.1 per cent in Siena and Lucca, and +4.6 per cent in Florence, Trieste, Verona, Vicenza and Syracuse. The categories most affected by price rises were electricity and gas, up 28.7 per cent; private transport, up 13.8 per cent; passenger transport services, up 9 per cent; mobile phones and computers, up 8.3 per cent; and accommodation services, up 6.1 per cent. This is according to the CGIA Research Department, based on an analysis of Istat data. The only categories to have recorded a fall in prices over the last eight months were vehicle purchases (-0.1 per cent), alcoholic drinks (-1.3 per cent), household appliances (-2.2 per cent) and package holidays (-8.1 per cent). Among the top 50 sub-categories with the highest price rises, the largest increases were seen in recording media (cassettes, video cassettes, DVDs, CDs) at +64.8 per cent; heating oil and kerosene for domestic use at +44.3 per cent; heating gas at +39.2 per cent, diesel at +32.2 per cent, electricity at +23.9 per cent, passenger air transport at +23.5 per cent and petrol at +22.7 per cent. At regional level, the sharpest rises were seen in Tuscany, up 4.2 per cent; followed by Sardinia and Veneto (both up 4 per cent). Donald Trump will discuss Iran, but not Ukraine, with his counterparts Xi Jinping and Vladimir Putin during the trilateral talks scheduled for next Thursday on the sidelines of the APEC summit in Shenzhen, China. This is according to the White House.

The leaders of the US, China and Russia, in their first-ever trilateral meeting, may also discuss their respective nuclear arsenals, according to a senior US official. The latest nuclear arms control treaty between Washington and Moscow expired in February, removing, for the first time in over half a century, the limits on the world’s two largest nuclear arsenals. When the agreement, known as ‘New Start’, expired, Trump rejected the Russian proposal to extend it by a year, calling instead for a “new, improved and modernised” deal that would also include China. The trilateral meeting is intended to be a “start to what we hope will be a conversation” on nuclear disarmament, “capable of leading to productive developments in the future”, the official added, noting that no announcements of agreements are expected. Beijing’s arsenal, which according to Pentagon estimates comprises over 600 warheads, is far smaller than that of the US and Russia, each of which possesses more than 5,000. Given this stark disparity, China has shown little interest in opening discussions on the issue, instead calling for a reduction in the number of warheads held by Washington and Moscow. The Trump administration recognises that, for Beijing, the issue may be complex: the official, however, described next week’s meeting as an opportunity for China to ‘take its place at the big table’ on a matter of international significance.

sources.title: Netanyahu says only a unity government can guarantee Israel’s security - Al Jazeera
passages: Israeli caretaker Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu has renewed his call for a national unity government with his rival, Gadi Eisenkot, saying only such a government can guarantee Israel’s security.

Under Eisenkot’s plan for a minority “national emergency government”, his bloc’s 48 lawmakers would vote in favour against the 46 Netanyahu supporters, while the 26 lawmakers from Arab and ultra-Orthodox parties could abstain.
It would allow his government to be approved without an absolute majority in the Knesset.
President Isaac Herzog last week tasked Eisenkot with forming a government, after 67 lawmakers, including those from Arab-led parties, endorsed him, while 46 backed Netanyahu.

Eisenkot has said he could work with members of Netanyahu’s Likud party and with Bezalel Smotrich’s Religious Zionism if their commitment to unity is “sincere”, but he insisted on a “break with the extremists”, notably supporters of far-right minister Itamar Ben-Gvir.
A former army chief, Eisenkot said Netanyahu “knows he lost the election”.
“Netanyahu is calling for negotiations while they are already underway,” he said.
Netanyahu’s version would include Jewish parties from the centre and the right and exclude Arab parties .
On Friday, Eisenkot called Netanyahu’s campaign against them “racist” .
The Knesset will elect its speaker on Tuesday.
The post is currently held by Netanyahu ally Amir Ohana, and the opposition has put forward Matan Kahana, a former military officer, in his place.

extraction.body: Eisenkot, in charge of forming a government, dismisses the appeal as ‘tricks’ as talks and a Knesset speaker vote loom. Israeli caretaker Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu has renewed his call for a national unity government with his rival, Gadi Eisenkot, saying only such a government can guarantee Israel’s security. In a video statement on Saturday, Netanyahu said a meeting with Eisenkot on Thursday “only strengthened the conviction that it is essential to form a national unity government”. The prime minister said such a government could “eliminate the Iranian threat once and for all”, claiming Tehran would “not hesitate to use nuclear weapons against us”. “Let’s meet in one room, without preconditions,” he said. Within minutes, however, Eisenkot dismissed the appeal as a ploy. A former army chief, Eisenkot said Netanyahu “knows he lost the election”. “Netanyahu is calling for negotiations while they are already underway,” he said. “These tricks don’t work on me.” Neither side won a majority in the October 27 election. Netanyahu’s right-wing and religious bloc took 53 seats in the 120-seat Knesset, Eisenkot’s four-party bloc got 48 seats, and Arab-led parties won a record 19. President Isaac Herzog last week tasked Eisenkot with forming a government, after 67 lawmakers, including those from Arab-led parties, endorsed him, while 46 backed Netanyahu. Eisenkot has 28 days, with a possible 14-day extension. He has ruled out including Arab-led parties in his government. Under Eisenkot’s plan for a minority “national emergency government”, his bloc’s 48 lawmakers would vote in favour against the 46 Netanyahu supporters, while the 26 lawmakers from Arab and ultra-Orthodox parties could abstain. It would allow his government to be approved without an absolute majority in the Knesset. Netanyahu has warned that such a government would lead to Israel’s “collapse”. Netanyahu’s version would include Jewish parties from the centre and the right and exclude Arab parties . He and his allies have made unsubstantiated claims that Arab-led parties “stole” the election. On Friday, Eisenkot called Netanyahu’s campaign against them “racist” . Eisenkot has said he could work with members of Netanyahu’s Likud party and with Bezalel Smotrich’s Religious Zionism if their commitment to unity is “sincere”, but he insisted on a “break with the extremists”, notably supporters of far-right minister Itamar Ben-Gvir. The Knesset will elect its speaker on Tuesday. The post is currently held by Netanyahu ally Amir Ohana, and the opposition has put forward Matan Kahana, a former military officer, in his place.

passages: Bitcoin's recent price decline caused $2.05 billion in liquidations across tracked crypto exchanges, with nearly $800 million occurring on Binance alone.
This widespread liquidation wave shows significant market activity concentrated on Binance but affecting multiple venues.
The event underscores the risks of bullish bets in volatile crypto markets and may signal further caution for investors.
Most liquidations were from traders betting on rising prices, highlighting a strong bearish move against bullish positions.

passages: The family of Banko Brown, the 24-year-old trans man shot and killed outside a Market Street Walgreens in 2023, will receive $5 million from the security guard who shot him and the guard's employer, according to a motion filed in San Francisco Superior Court on Thursday, November 12, 2026.

The settlement resolves claims against the guard, Michael Earl-Wayne Anthony, and his employer, Kingdom Group Protective Services, while claims against Walgreens, Walgreens Boots Alliance and Allied Universal Security Services remain unresolved.
The wrongful-death case had sought at least $25 million in damages and helped push the city to rewrite its rules on armed security guards.
Ben Nisenbaum, the attorney representing Brown's parents, Terry Brown and Kevinisha Henderson, confirmed that both sides had agreed to the settlement, per the same report.
Brown's killing sparked nationwide outrage and fueled a movement to disarm city security guards and overhaul armed-guard training.
His family rallied and marched to San Francisco City Hall after his death.
The San Francisco Standard reported that attorneys for Brown's family said he had been attempting to steal about $14 worth of food items, while SFist described the items as $15 worth of candy.

A Kingdom executive said Walgreens store management at individual locations frequently pressured security officers to violate Kingdom policies, and a court email cited in the complaint shows Walgreens directed Kingdom guards across Northern California to begin stopping shoplifters starting April 13, 2023 — just two weeks before Brown was killed.

extraction.body: The family of Banko Brown, the 24-year-old trans man shot and killed outside a Market Street Walgreens in 2023, will receive $5 million from the security guard who shot him and the guard's employer, according to a motion filed in San Francisco Superior Court on Thursday, November 12, 2026. The settlement resolves claims against the guard, Michael Earl-Wayne Anthony, and his employer, Kingdom Group Protective Services, while claims against Walgreens, Walgreens Boots Alliance and Allied Universal Security Services remain unresolved. The wrongful-death case had sought at least $25 million in damages and helped push the city to rewrite its rules on armed security guards. According to SFGATE , Brown's family will get the $5 million from guard Michael Earl-Wayne Anthony and his employer, Kingdom Group Protective Services. Ben Nisenbaum, the attorney representing Brown's parents, Terry Brown and Kevinisha Henderson, confirmed that both sides had agreed to the settlement, per the same report. The settlement terms include complete dismissal of the complaint against Kingdom and Anthony, though Walgreens, Walgreens Boots Alliance and Allied Universal Security Services have not reached a settlement agreement with the family, the outlet notes. Brown was shot on April 27, 2023, outside the Walgreens on Market Street in downtown San Francisco after allegedly shoplifting snacks and getting into a brief argument with Anthony. The wrongful-death complaint, filed by Nisenbaum's firm, Burris, Nisenbaum, Curry and Lacy, states that Brown stood 5-foot-4, weighed about 155 pounds, and was unarmed when he was killed. Brown had grown up in San Francisco and organized with the Young Women's Freedom Center, which supports women and trans youth. Accounts of the alleged shoplifting differ on the value of what Brown was accused of trying to take. The San Francisco Standard reported that attorneys for Brown's family said he had been attempting to steal about $14 worth of food items, while SFist described the items as $15 worth of candy. District Attorney Brooke Jenkins declined to bring charges against Anthony, finding that he believed he was in mortal danger and acted in self-defense, the Standard reported at the time. The wrongful-death complaint, dated May 25, 2023, named Anthony, Kingdom Group Protective Services, Allied Universal Security Services, Walgreens and Walgreens Boots Alliance as responsible parties, and it alleged negligent hiring, training and supervision of Anthony. Anthony had started working with Kingdom in 2022 and received all of his security guard training over Zoom, according to the complaint. A Kingdom executive said Walgreens store management at individual locations frequently pressured security officers to violate Kingdom policies, and a court email cited in the complaint shows Walgreens directed Kingdom guards across Northern California to begin stopping shoplifters starting April 13, 2023 — just two weeks before Brown was killed. Brown's killing sparked nationwide outrage and fueled a movement to disarm city security guards and overhaul armed-guard training. His family rallied and marched to San Francisco City Hall after his death. Kingdom security guards were disarmed at Walgreens stores in San Francisco by May 4, 2023, and the company was removed as the contracted security provider at the store later that year. Walgreens ultimately canceled its contract with Kingdom entirely, per the Standard. In October 2023, the San Francisco Board of Supervisors voted to amend the city's police code so that armed guards could only draw their firearms in response to a threat to a person, not to protect property, SFist reported. Under San Francisco Police Code § 1750.19, drawing a firearm is unlawful except in response to an actual and specific threat to a person or persons. The $5 million settlement resolves the claims against Anthony and Kingdom, but the case against Walgreens, Walgreens Boots Alliance and Allied Universal Security Services remains unresolved, as those parties have not reached an agreement with Brown's family. coreStoryFacts.text: The family of Banko Brown, the 24-year-old trans man shot and killed outside a Market Street Walgreens in 2023, will receive $5 million from the security guard who shot him and the guard's employer, according to a motion filed in San Francisco Superior Court on Thursday, November 12, 2026.

The settlement resolves claims against the guard, Michael Earl-Wayne Anthony, and his employer, Kingdom Group Protective Services, while claims against Walgreens, Walgreens Boots Alliance and Allied Universal Security Services remain unresolved.
The wrongful-death case had sought at least $25 million in damages and helped push the city to rewrite its rules on armed security guards.
Ben Nisenbaum, the attorney representing Brown's parents, Terry Brown and Kevinisha Henderson, confirmed that both sides had agreed to the settlement, per the same report.
Brown's killing sparked nationwide outrage and fueled a movement to disarm city security guards and overhaul armed-guard training.
His family rallied and marched to San Francisco City Hall after his death.
The San Francisco Standard reported that attorneys for Brown's family said he had been attempting to steal about $14 worth of food items, while SFist described the items as $15 worth of candy.

A Kingdom executive said Walgreens store management at individual locations frequently pressured security officers to violate Kingdom policies, and a court email cited in the complaint shows Walgreens directed Kingdom guards across Northern California to begin stopping shoplifters starting April 13, 2023 — just two weeks before Brown was killed.

extraction.body: The Chip Security Act is getting renewed attention following Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang’s resignation and reported affair with an alleged Chinese spy. Representatives from Nvidia told Illinois representative Bill Foster that it would be technically possible to implement the anti-smuggling measures called for in the Chip Security Act, Foster told MIT Technology Review in an interview on Thursday, even while an industry group claimed they were “potentially infeasible.” Foster, a Democrat who serves on the Committee on Science, Space, and Technology, is a cosponsor of the act, which would introduce geotracking requirements to verify the location of advanced AI chips in order to prevent their smuggling to China. It is one of three chip-security bills under consideration for inclusion in the Senate’s National Defense Authorization Act, each of which is drawing renewed attention after Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang’s resignation and reported affair with an alleged Chinese spy. When the Chip Security Act was introduced, in May 2025, lawmakers said the technology to implement it existed, something Nvidia has not publicly confirmed. In March 2026, the Semiconductor Industry Association, of which Nvidia is a member, explicitly opposed the bill and wrote that its mandates for chip tracking were “new, untested, and potentially infeasible.” But privately, Nvidia representatives working with Foster told the lawmaker that the company could implement them. “They never put anything in writing,” Foster says, but during technical discussions on the possibility of such safeguards, their reaction was “yeah, of course we can do this.” This private acknowledgment to Foster goes further than anything Nvidia has previously made public. Other technology Nvidia has built for its customers suggests that the company can indeed offer accurate tracking of its chips’ locations. In December 2025, for example, it announced a new tool called Fleet Intelligence that would allow customers to monitor how its advanced chips were performing across different data center locations. In doing so, the tool could indicate which country chips were in, Nvidia confirmed to Reuters, but the company would not elaborate on whether this technology could be used to prevent smuggling. Nvidia did not respond to requests for comment or confirmation of Foster’s characterization. In early October, when lawmakers were reportedly increasingly concerned about Nvidia’s role in smuggling, MIT Technology Review asked the company if Fleet Intelligence could be used to prevent the practice. It declined to answer directly, instead sending a statement: “Governments and media have found insignificant diversion of controlled US products—a drop in the bucket compared to the ocean of domestic compute China already has.” The recent fallout at Nvidia involves a number of people and companies alleged to be involved in chip smuggling. Alice Huang, with whom Jensen Huang reportedly had an affair, runs Megaspeed, a Singaporean firm now under investigation for smuggling advanced GPUs to China. A US Commerce Department inquiry into the company was reportedly halted after invention by Nvidia. Megaspeed reportedly bought chips from Supermicro, a company that packages Nvidia’s chips onto servers. The Chip Security Act as drafted would require a mechanism to track the locations of chips, either by inspections of facilities, attestations by companies, or ping-based location mechanisms. The ping-based technique, the hardest option to circumvent, would require the GPU to send a signal of its location when it comes online. In September, the Center for Security and Emerging Technology found it would be the most cost-effective option. Foster said he did not ask Nvidia’s representatives why they weren’t voluntarily adopting such chip-tracking tools if they could technically do so. But if the requirements of the bill pass as part of the Senate’s National Defense Authorization Act, the new tracking mechanisms would only tell investigators where the chips are, not offer a way to disconnect them if it’s revealed they have been smuggled. Foster told MIT Technology Review he intends to introduce new, stricter legislation in the new year that would offer a workaround. The new rule would require licenses to operate advanced GPUs, and before a GPU could connect, its valid license would need to be verified. In the meantime, the controversy at Nvidia, Foster says, has fueled support among his colleagues for the rules in the bill: “There will be a lot of political pressure, in the wake of everything that’s happened, on the companies to actually do a very good job of the geographic validation of where the chip actually is.” Ten years after AlphaGo’s match against Go champion Lee Sedol, today’s AI still isn’t tapping into the machinery that made that win possible.

Representatives from Nvidia told Illinois representative Bill Foster that it would be technically possible to implement the anti-smuggling measures called for in the Chip Security Act, Foster told MIT Technology Review in an interview on Thursday, even while an industry group claimed they were “potentially infeasible.”

Foster, a Democrat who serves on the Committee on Science, Space, and Technology, is a cosponsor of the act, which would introduce geotracking requirements to verify the location of advanced AI chips in order to prevent their smuggling to China. It is one of three chip-security bills under consideration for inclusion in the Senate’s National Defense Authorization Act, each of which is drawing renewed attention after Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang’s resignation and reported affair with an alleged Chinese spy.

When the Chip Security Act was introduced, in May 2025, lawmakers said the technology to implement it existed, something Nvidia has not publicly confirmed. In March 2026, the Semiconductor Industry Association, of which Nvidia is a member, explicitly opposed the bill and wrote that its mandates for chip tracking were “new, untested, and potentially infeasible.”
But privately, Nvidia representatives working with Foster told the lawmaker that the company could implement them.

“They never put anything in writing,” Foster says, but during technical discussions on the possibility of such safeguards, their reaction was “yeah, of course we can do this.” This private acknowledgment to Foster goes further than anything Nvidia has previously made public.

Other technology Nvidia has built for its customers suggests that the company can indeed offer accurate tracking of its chips’ locations. In December 2025, for example, it announced a new tool called Fleet Intelligence that would allow customers to monitor how its advanced chips were performing across different data center locations. In doing so, the tool could indicate which country chips were in, Nvidia confirmed to Reuters, but the company would not elaborate on whether this technology could be used to prevent smuggling.
Nvidia did not respond to requests for comment or confirmation of Foster’s characterization.

In early October, when lawmakers were reportedly increasingly concerned about Nvidia’s role in smuggling, MIT Technology Review asked the company if Fleet Intelligence could be used to prevent the practice. It declined to answer directly, instead sending a statement: “Governments and media have found insignificant diversion of controlled US products—a drop in the bucket compared to the ocean of domestic compute China already has.”

The recent fallout at Nvidia involves a number of people and companies alleged to be involved in chip smuggling. Alice Huang, with whom Jensen Huang reportedly had an affair, runs Megaspeed, a Singaporean firm now under investigation for smuggling advanced GPUs to China. A US Commerce Department inquiry into the company was reportedly halted after invention by Nvidia. Megaspeed reportedly bought chips from Supermicro, a company that packages Nvidia’s chips onto servers.

The Chip Security Act as drafted would require a mechanism to track the locations of chips, either by inspections of facilities, attestations by companies, or ping-based location mechanisms. The ping-based technique, the hardest option to circumvent, would require the GPU to send a signal of its location when it comes online. In September, the Center for Security and Emerging Technology found it would be the most cost-effective option.
Foster said he did not ask Nvidia’s representatives why they weren’t voluntarily adopting such chip-tracking tools if they could technically do so.

But if the requirements of the bill pass as part of the Senate’s National Defense Authorization Act, the new tracking mechanisms would only tell investigators where the chips are, not offer a way to disconnect them if it’s revealed they have been smuggled. Foster told MIT Technology Review he intends to introduce new, stricter legislation in the new year that would offer a workaround. The new rule would require licenses to operate advanced GPUs, and before a GPU could connect, its valid license would need to be verified.

In the meantime, the controversy at Nvidia, Foster says, has fueled support among his colleagues for the rules in the bill: “There will be a lot of political pressure, in the wake of everything that’s happened, on the companies to actually do a very good job of the geographic validation of where the chip actually is.”
Ten years after AlphaGo’s match against Go champion Lee Sedol, today’s AI still isn’t tapping into the machinery that made that win possible.

passages: Nvidia representatives privately told a member of Congress that the company could technically meet the anti-smuggling requirements of the Chip Security Act, even as the chip industry publicly argued those requirements might be infeasible, MIT Technology Review reported on Thursday, Nov. 12 [1] . Rep. Bill Foster, an Illinois Democrat and co-sponsor of the bill, said that in informal technical discussions Nvidia's reaction was "yeah, of course we can do this" [1] .

"They never put anything in writing," Foster told the publication [1] . Nvidia did not respond to requests for comment or to confirm his account [1] . The report lands as Congress weighs writing chip-export limits into the annual defense bill in the wake of the scandal that ended Jensen Huang's tenure as Nvidia's chief executive.

The Chip Security Act, introduced in May 2025, would require companies to verify where advanced AI chips end up after export [1] . As drafted, that could be done through facility inspections, company attestations or a ping-based mechanism in which a GPU sends a location signal when it comes online, MIT Technology Review reported [1] . The ping-based option is the hardest to get around, and a September study by Georgetown's Center for Security and Emerging Technology found it would be the most cost-effective, according to the report [1] .

The tracking would show where chips are but would not let anyone switch them off remotely [1] . Foster told MIT Technology Review he plans stricter legislation next year that would require a licence to operate advanced GPUs, verified before a GPU can connect [1] . He said he had not asked Nvidia why, if tracking is technically possible, it has not adopted it voluntarily [1] .

The Semiconductor Industry Association, whose members include Nvidia, opposed the bill in March, saying its chip-tracking mandates were "new, untested, and potentially infeasible" [1] . Nvidia itself has played down smuggling. In October it told MIT Technology Review that "governments and media have found insignificant diversion of controlled US products," calling it "a drop in the bucket compared to the ocean of domestic compute China already has" [1] .

The company has already built part of the capability. In December 2025, Reuters reported, citing people familiar with the matter, that Nvidia had privately demonstrated an optional software update that would use the time delay in communicating with Nvidia-run servers to gauge a chip's location, starting with Blackwell chips [2] . Nvidia said then that it was "in the process of implementing a new software service" for fleet monitoring, and it has denied that its chips have backdoors [2] . Nvidia has told Reuters the tool can indicate which country chips are in but would not say whether it could prevent smuggling, MIT Technology Review reported [1] .

The Chip Security Act is one of three chip measures in the Senate's version of the fiscal 2027 National Defense Authorization Act, alongside the MATCH Act and the AI Overwatch Act [1] [3] . Senate Majority Leader John Thune told Semafor on Thursday there is a "high probability" that Congress will impose more restrictions on chip exports to China, though no deal has been reached to keep the measures in the final bill [3] . MLQ.ai's analysis of the bills and rules in play and its report on the Justice Department and congressional fallout set out where each stands.

Smuggling is the issue at the center of the scandal. Megaspeed, the Singapore cloud company whose former executive Alice Huang was reportedly in a relationship with Jensen Huang, has been investigated by US authorities over suspicions it helped Chinese companies obtain restricted chips; it has denied smuggling [1] [4] . A Commerce Department inquiry into Megaspeed was halted after Nvidia's general counsel contacted Commerce agents, The New York Times reported [4] . US officials suspect Alice Huang of spying for Beijing, which China denies, as MLQ.ai's coverage of Huang's resignation sets out [5] .

However, Bitcoin closed at $58,566 on June 30, just under that call and 11% below it, marking its lowest close in the past year.

Galaxy Research took the opposite view on the same day. Its cycle study, which looked at where analysts say Bitcoin bottoms, expected a fourth-quarter bottom between $40,000 and $46,000, 30% to 39% below Bitcoin's price. In a softer outlook, the firm suggested a low between $51,000 and $54,000.

Middle Scenario ($65,000 to $73,000). In this case, Bitcoin holds above its June low but remains below its 200-day moving average of $73,043, about 11% above its price. Slower outflows following an expected Fed rate hike would fit this scenario.

High Scenario ($80,000 to $84,000). To reach this range, Bitcoin must climb above its 50-day average of $80,558, about 22% above its price. That may require a turnaround in ETF flows similar to August's inflow of about $3.5 billion. passages: It was the resignation heard across the world.
Jensen Huang, Nvidia’s embattled CEO who co-founded and led the company for 33 years, had officially stepped down .
“It’s like a bomb went off,” one neocloud founder told TechCrunch when he first heard the news.
Most of the significant decisions to invest in startups often came from Jensen himself, according to Umesh Padval, managing partner at Seligman Ventures.

Huang’s absence leaves the startup ecosystem without one of its biggest champions and with far less capital for now, investors say, which could have a massive impact on dealmaking, valuations, funding, and even competition.

If the company does grow more conservative with its startup investments, that could leave more room for rivals and smaller competitors. (Coincidentally, Google announced two new chips this week amid Huang’s Nvidia fallout.)
“When Nvidia was on the cap table, everyone felt safe,” Padval said.
Without that backing, investors say traditional VCs are likely to think twice before writing checks into these startups and may even pause certain dealmaking.
“Jensen’s initiatives are a big reason an ecosystem has emerged despite that,” Zain Javaid, founder of the hardware company Ghost, said.
Some investors with whom TechCrunch spoke hope that large cloud companies and other chipmakers will step in to back startups and fill some of the void that will likely be left by Huang.

extraction.body: It was the resignation heard across the world. Jensen Huang, Nvidia’s embattled CEO who co-founded and led the company for 33 years, had officially stepped down . “It’s like a bomb went off,” one neocloud founder told TechCrunch when he first heard the news. Over the last several years, Nvidia has been a prolific investor , pouring tens of billions into startups annually and participating in 105 rounds this year alone, often as the largest investor, according to PitchBook. “If that direction changes, it’ll be a big blow to so many young companies,” said Maria Davidson, founder of Relational Capital. Huang’s absence leaves the startup ecosystem without one of its biggest champions and with far less capital for now, investors say, which could have a massive impact on dealmaking, valuations, funding, and even competition. “Nvidia is carrying almost every AI-native startup from application to neocloud,” Dawn Capital’s Shamillah Bankiya told TechCrunch. Most of the significant decisions to invest in startups often came from Jensen himself, according to Umesh Padval, managing partner at Seligman Ventures. Padval has known Huang since serving on the board of Mellanox Technologies, a networking chipmaker Nvidia acquired for approximately $7 billion in 2020. While there is hope that Huang’s eventual successor will resume his dealmaking spree, investors aren’t hopeful that it will happen in the short term. Nvidia’s interim CEO, Colette Kress, is expected to institute some changes , especially when it comes to Nvidia’s investments into AI startups at the crux of the billion-dollar data center build-out . Huang’s rampant dealmaking in this sphere has been a source of concern for Wall Street. “She’s much more conservative,” one investor said of Kress. “I don’t think she’s going to commit the same amount of money to keep the early-stage ecosystem going.” Nvidia’s biggest bets were backing neoclouds, inference providers, and open weight models, which are expensive for smaller companies to build. “Jensen’s initiatives are a big reason an ecosystem has emerged despite that,” Zain Javaid, founder of the hardware company Ghost, said. For instance, Nvidia backed CoreWeave when it was still private and participated in two of Crusoe’s rounds, including its $1.4 billion Series E. It bought Hugging Face this year for $13 billion (expected to close in 2027) and holds investments in Mistral AI, Lambda, and Black Forest Labs. Nvidia was often the largest investor in the deals. Last year, it wrote an $800 million check into a $2 billion Series B round for Reflection AI, before the open source startup began to earn meaningful revenue, according to the Wall Street Journal . “Jensen believed in open source and frankly speaking, Europe,” Bankiya said of how Huang invested so much in AI across the world. The cease of that support in other regions outside of America, like Europe “would be a massive funding and honestly ecosystem gap that no one can fill.” It’s also true that Nvidia was such a dominant player in the ecosystem that at times, it felt like a monopoly. By backing so many companies with such generous checks, Nvidia effectively locked those startups into using its chips, which helped reinforce its dominant market position. If the company does grow more conservative with its startup investments, that could leave more room for rivals and smaller competitors. (Coincidentally, Google announced two new chips this week amid Huang’s Nvidia fallout.) Some investors with whom TechCrunch spoke hope that large cloud companies and other chipmakers will step in to back startups and fill some of the void that will likely be left by Huang. Dharmesh Thakker, a general partner at Battery Ventures, for example, expects Big Tech rivals to vie for Nvidia’s investment crown, “depending upon who brings the best combination of a great product, an ecosystem and community to compete with CUDA, and the financial power to bankroll the ecosystem,” he said. CUDA is Nvidia’s software platform that enables developers to run AI models on its GPUs. While companies like Google, Amazon, Microsoft, and AMD may back mature startups to drive adoption of their chips and clouds, Thakker doubts they will pour hundreds of millions into pre-revenue infrastructure startups the way Nvidia did. Under Huang, infrastructure companies that needed $100 million to $500 million in GPUs would often raise half of that amount at valuations of $1 billion or more from Nvidia just to get started, one VC said. The chipmaker’s participation gave other investors the comfort in backing these companies at the lofty valuations. Now Nvidia is expected to be more selective in the new companies it backs, while writing smaller-sized checks into its existing portfolio, contributing to a drop in valuations. “When Nvidia was on the cap table, everyone felt safe,” Padval said. Without that backing, investors say traditional VCs are likely to think twice before writing checks into these startups and may even pause certain dealmaking. Even so, few believe that Nvidia’s investment slowdown will by itself halt the broader AI boom. Though everyone agrees that Huang is a massive loss for Nvidia, one of his ex-employees, Amulya Vishwanath, who now runs her own VC fund, said that “founders and leaders must be held accountable,” and that the ecosystem is bigger than one person. “That talent will, and must, continue to thrive.” Dominic-Madori Davis is a senior venture capital and startup reporter at TechCrunch. extraction.body: It was the resignation heard across the world. Jensen Huang, Nvidia’s embattled CEO who co-founded and led the company for 33 years, had officially stepped down . “It’s like a bomb went off,” one neocloud founder told TechCrunch when he first heard the news. Over the last several years, Nvidia has been a prolific investor , pouring tens of billions into startups annually and participating in 105 rounds this year alone, often as the largest investor, according to PitchBook. “If that direction changes, it’ll be a big blow to so many young companies,” said Maria Davidson, founder of Relational Capital. Huang’s absence leaves the startup ecosystem without one of its biggest champions and with far less capital for now, investors say, which could have a massive impact on dealmaking, valuations, funding, and even competition. “Nvidia is carrying almost every AI-native startup from application to neocloud,” Dawn Capital’s Shamillah Bankiya told TechCrunch. Most of the significant decisions to invest in startups often came from Jensen himself, according to Umesh Padval, managing partner at Seligman Ventures. Padval has known Huang since serving on the board of Mellanox Technologies, a networking chipmaker Nvidia acquired for approximately $7 billion in 2020. While there is hope that Huang’s eventual successor will resume his dealmaking spree, investors aren’t hopeful that it will happen in the short term. Nvidia’s interim CEO, Colette Kress, is expected to institute some changes , especially when it comes to Nvidia’s investments into AI startups at the crux of the billion-dollar data center build-out . Huang’s rampant dealmaking in this sphere has been a source of concern for Wall Street. “She’s much more conservative,” one investor said of Kress. “I don’t think she’s going to commit the same amount of money to keep the early-stage ecosystem going.” Nvidia’s biggest bets were backing neoclouds, inference providers, and open weight models, which are expensive for smaller companies to build. “Jensen’s initiatives are a big reason an ecosystem has emerged despite that,” Zain Javaid, founder of the hardware company Ghost, said. For instance, Nvidia backed CoreWeave when it was still private and participated in two of Crusoe’s rounds, including its $1.4 billion Series E. It bought Hugging Face this year for $13 billion (expected to close in 2027) and holds investments in Mistral AI, Lambda, and Black Forest Labs. Nvidia was often the largest investor in the deals. Last year, it wrote an $800 million check into a $2 billion Series B round for Reflection AI, before the open source startup began to earn meaningful revenue, according to the Wall Street Journal . “Jensen believed in open source and frankly speaking, Europe,” Bankiya said of how Huang invested so much in AI across the world. The cease of that support in other regions outside of America, like Europe “would be a massive funding and honestly ecosystem gap that no one can fill.” It’s also true that Nvidia was such a dominant player in the ecosystem that at times, it felt like a monopoly. By backing so many companies with such generous checks, Nvidia effectively locked those startups into using its chips, which helped reinforce its dominant market position. If the company does grow more conservative with its startup investments, that could leave more room for rivals and smaller competitors. (Coincidentally, Google announced two new chips this week amid Huang’s Nvidia fallout.) Some investors with whom TechCrunch spoke hope that large cloud companies and other chipmakers will step in to back startups and fill some of the void that will likely be left by Huang. Dharmesh Thakker, a general partner at Battery Ventures, for example, expects Big Tech rivals to vie for Nvidia’s investment crown, “depending upon who brings the best combination of a great product, an ecosystem and community to compete with CUDA, and the financial power to bankroll the ecosystem,” he said. CUDA is Nvidia’s software platform that enables developers to run AI models on its GPUs. While companies like Google, Amazon, Microsoft, and AMD may back mature startups to drive adoption of their chips and clouds, Thakker doubts they will pour hundreds of millions into pre-revenue infrastructure startups the way Nvidia did. Under Huang, infrastructure companies that needed $100 million to $500 million in GPUs would often raise half of that amount at valuations of $1 billion or more from Nvidia just to get started, one VC said. The chipmaker’s participation gave other investors the comfort in backing these companies at the lofty valuations. Now Nvidia is expected to be more selective in the new companies it backs, while writing smaller-sized checks into its existing portfolio, contributing to a drop in valuations. “When Nvidia was on the cap table, everyone felt safe,” Padval said. Without that backing, investors say traditional VCs are likely to think twice before writing checks into these startups and may even pause certain dealmaking. Even so, few believe that Nvidia’s investment slowdown will by itself halt the broader AI boom. Though everyone agrees that Huang is a massive loss for Nvidia, one of his ex-employees, Amulya Vishwanath, who now runs her own VC fund, said that “founders and leaders must be held accountable,” and that the ecosystem is bigger than one person. “That talent will, and must, continue to thrive.” Dominic-Madori Davis is a senior venture capital and startup reporter at TechCrunch. She is based in New York City. You can contact or verify outreach from Dominic by emailing [email protected] or via encrypted message at +1 646 831-7565 on Signal. To reach the top end of the forecast range by December 31, Bitcoin would need to rally 21%.

Sellers have dominated the market for weeks. Bitcoin reached $84,082 on October 21 and has dropped 20.4% over the past 30 days, including a 4.3% decline in the last 24 hours. Research firm Bespoke noted that Bitcoin is “deep into oversold territory,” suggesting that selling pressure might soon ease. So where might Bitcoin stand at year-end?

Bitcoin’s market cap is about $1.33 trillion, with roughly 20.1 million coins in circulation and a maximum supply of 21 million. As new coins are mined, the same price now represents a larger total market value than in previous cycles. If Bitcoin reaches $80,000, its market cap would be about $1.61 trillion, and returning to its all-time high would push it to around $2.54 trillion.

Investor sentiment has also shifted, with money moving out of Bitcoin funds. According to SoSoValue, spot Bitcoin ETFs —funds that directly hold Bitcoin—have $89.6 billion in assets but saw net outflows of $2.14 billion over the past 30 days.

All of these forecasts were made before the latest market downturn. Geoffrey Kendrick, then Standard Chartered’s global head of digital assets research, stated on June 12 that Bitcoin had already hit its bottom at $59,000. However, Bitcoin closed at $58,566 on June 30, just under that call and 11% below it, marking its lowest close in the past year.

Galaxy Research took the opposite view on the same day. Its cycle study, which looked at where analysts say Bitcoin bottoms , expected a fourth-quarter bottom between $40,000 and $46,000, 30% to 39% below Bitcoin’s price. In a softer outlook, the firm suggested a low between $51,000 and $54,000.

On the upside, the $80,000 mark remains a recurring target. A market observer urged caution around that level on September 18, emphasizing the need for positive ETF flows. A Bitcoin price prediction for November suggested that if Bitcoin held above $76,141, it could trade between $76,000 and $82,000, but Bitcoin has since fallen below $76,141.

The likelihood of Bitcoin hitting $80,000 by December 31 appears low, with the most probable year-end price between $65,000 and $73,000. The Federal Reserve, which raised the top of its target range to 4% on September 16, is scheduled to meet again on December 9, and fed funds futures, contracts that track rate expectations, place an 89% probability on another quarter-point hike. Since reaching $86,597 on September 21, Bitcoin’s price has trended downward.

A key level to monitor is $58,566. A close below it after the Fed’s December 9 decision could make the low scenario more likely, while a Fed pause and a rise above $73,043 might revive the high scenario. Over a longer horizon, Bitcoin is up 72.5% over the past three years, and a look at how much one Bitcoin could be worth in 2030 takes that longer view.

Sam has written about crypto professionally since 2019 and has published more than 2,000 articles. Before joining 24/7 Wall St., he wrote for crypto media outlets and Web3 companies and ghostwrote for crypto founders and token launches. His analysis is syndicated on Yahoo Finance, MSN and AOL and has been cited by other crypto news sites. He also founded MacLabs Marketing, a content and personal branding agency for crypto founders and executives. When he isn't reading charts, Sam is usually at the gym or watching One Piece, a series he maintains has better tokenomics than most altcoins.

Holders keep coming back to one recovery number: the September rally high of $87,397. If Bitcoin can get back there, the 2026 rebound held. History points the other way. One year after its 2013, 2017 and 2021 peaks, Bitcoin was down about 70%, 82% and 75%, according to a CoinDesk cycle comparison.
So the question is whether Bitcoin can reclaim $87,397 in 2027, or whether this decline still has further to fall.

At today's price, Bitcoin's market cap (price multiplied by coins in circulation) is about $1.34 trillion. It is still the No. 1 crypto asset. The coin sits 47.27% below the record of $126,080, set on October 6, 2025. It is down 29.85% over the past year and 24.08% year to date.

The climb is harder than the chart suggests because of supply dilution. Miners create new bitcoin with every block they add, so the circulating supply keeps growing. Bitcoin is up just 4.11% from $63,857.77 five years ago. The network is worth more today than it was at that price, because more coins exist. The same logic applies going forward. Every return to an old price level takes more new dollars than the previous visit did.

This cycle has been softer than past ones so far. A one-year loss of about 30% is a long way from 70% or more. But 2022 shows that the first flush is often not the last. Bitcoin hit a June 2022 low of $17,697.70 and then broke lower to $15,598.50 in November. This year already produced a June closing low of $58,566.09. Riding a mania on the way up is one skill; knowing when to step aside is another, and we wrote a free handbook on both halves of that trade.

Spot Bitcoin ETFs are funds that hold actual bitcoin and trade like stocks. Their cumulative net inflow, meaning all the money that has come in minus all the money that has gone out, peaked at $57.96 billion on October 21. By November 13 it had dropped to $54.63 billion. Total net assets fell from $109.31 billion to $86.20 billion over the same period. The last three sessions all lost money: $299.90 million, $284.00 million and $185.45 million. The worst day was October 30, with $643.33 million in outflows.

Flows have moved the price before. Inflows of $526.60 million on October 19 and $528.40 million on October 21 came right before the 30-day high that same week. We covered how fast that reversed in our October look at ETF outflows.

The 10-year Treasury yield reached 5.10% on November 12, up from 4.84% on November 5. The Fed's target rate has an upper limit of 4.00%, unchanged over the past month. Goldman Sachs ( NYSE:GS ) added another rate hike to its Fed outlook after hot inflation data. When a government bond pays 5% with no risk, an asset that pays no yield, like Bitcoin, has to compete for that money. Liquidity has kept growing all the same: M2, a broad measure of money in the economy, was up 5.7% year over year as of September. That money is going somewhere other than Bitcoin.

On November 13, CoinDesk reported about $1.64 billion in crypto futures liquidations over 24 hours, most of them long positions (trades that profit when prices rise). Prediction markets are pricing more damage. On Kalshi, traders see a 23% chance that Bitcoin falls below $55,000 before January 1, 2027, and a 15% chance it falls below $50,000. They give it a 4% chance of exceeding $100,000 by year-end.

Bitcoin has a low chance of getting back to $87,397 in 2027 unless three things happen in this order. First, ETF flows need to stay positive long enough to push cumulative inflows back above $57.96 billion. Second, the 10-year yield needs to fall back toward its early-November low of 4.84%. Third, the price needs to recover its 200-day moving average (the average closing price over the past 200 days) of $73,043.04, then its 50-day average of $80,558.31. Until Bitcoin closes above $73,043, $87,397 is not a realistic target.

If flows stay negative and yields hold above 5%, the June closing low of $58,566.09 is the level to watch. Closing below it on a daily basis would put Bitcoin on the same path as 2022, where the second low came in below the first. Keep an eye on two triggers: settling above $73,043 means the recovery case is back, and a close below $58,566 means the worst is still ahead.

Bitcoin and the broader cryptocurrency market could face near-term volatility following Democrats' takeover of Congress. But Bitwise Chief Investment Officer Matt Hougan believes younger, crypto-friendly lawmakers will still support the industry's long-term growth. In his weekly memo on Nov. 11, Hougan argued that the election changed the political balance of Congress without significantly weakening support for digital assets. "The election doesn't matter for crypto; demographics do," he wrote. Credit Card Debt Is Getting Harder to Shake. 4 Steps to Take Before Your Balance Gets Even Bigger Hougan highlighted data from crypto advocacy group "Stand With Crypto" showing that the incoming Congress retains substantial support for digital assets. 51 pro-crypto senators: Just one fewer than the outgoing Congress. 241 pro-crypto House members: Already a majority of the 425-member caucus cited in the memo. 15 senators under 50: Nearly double the previous eight. Incoming senators are also 14 years younger on average than those leaving office. Hougan argued that younger politicians are more comfortable with cryptocurrencies because they grew up alongside digital technology. He cited a "Charles Schwab survey" showing that 33% of millennials own crypto, compared with just 8% of Baby Boomers. "Congress turned blue, but it also turned less grey," Hougan said. See Also: Trump Wants America to Lead the Crypto Race. Here's 4 Things Investors Should Watch as the Industry Changes Hougan expects greater scrutiny of Trump-linked crypto ventures, prediction markets and the broader industry, particularly if Sen. Elizabeth Warren (D-Mass.) leads the Senate Banking Committee. However, Bitcoin, stablecoins and tokenization will remain resilient. He highlighted newly elected Texas Democratic Sen. James Talarico , 37, who holds an A rating from "Stand With Crypto" and backed a Texas Bitcoin reserve. Hougan expects political uncertainty to create volatility over the coming weeks and potentially months. Although, he views election-driven weakness as a potential buying opportunity, arguing that generational adoption matters more than which party controls Congress. His thesis is that younger lawmakers will increasingly shape crypto policy as they gain political influence. Still Learning the Market? Economic cycles shift, sectors rise and fall, and no one investment performs well in every environment. By spreading exposure across multiple asset classes, it becomes easier to manage risk, capture steady returns, and create long-term wealth that isn't tied to the fortunes of just one company or industry. For accredited investors looking beyond stocks and bonds, EquityMultiple provides access to vetted commercial real estate deals starting at $5,000 , with only ~5% of opportunities passing their due diligence process. Backed by Jeff Bezos, Arrived Homes makes real estate investing accessible with a low barrier to entry. Investors can buy fractional shares of single-family rentals and vacation homes starting with as little as $100 . This allows everyday investors to diversify into real estate, collect rental income, and build long-term wealth without needing to manage properties directly. As AI coding tools take on more of the work traditionally done by developers, companies are facing new challenges around code quality, context and the rising cost of AI-powered development. Bito is building software designed to help AI coding agents better understand complex codebases while helping companies control AI development costs. Founded by former PubMatic executives, Bito has raised more than $10 million from institutional and individual investors and is now raising additional capital through a Wefunder offering, giving investors an opportunity to invest in a company targeting an emerging need within the rapidly expanding AI software market. Farmland has historically held its value through market volatility and delivered returns uncorrelated to stocks and bonds.
